title: props-as-blocks: registry-backed `::` input flow + property-name enforcement at the write seam
description:
Two halves of the same surface: **where a property name gets authored**, and how a user creates a property at all once a workspace is child-backed. Split out of the props-as-blocks §11 work-items list so it has a tracker rather than living in prose.

Context: PR #436 landed the `::` grammar — a field row's content is `::` + one reference span (`::((fieldId))`, `::[[Alias]]`, `::[label](((uuid)))`). Spec: [§7 grammar box + §9 recognition](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/blob/master/docs/properties-as-blocks-migration.html).

## 1. Registry-backed `::` input flow (not started)

Post-flip there is **no way to create a property except typing a raw definition UUID**. The kernel mints `::((fieldId))` correctly and recognition works, but nothing in the UI offers it.

Wanted: typing `::` in a block opens a registry-backed autocomplete over the workspace's property definitions (the same registry `PropertyPicker` reads), and picking one rewrites the block's content to `::((fieldId))` — id-addressed, so it stays rename-stable. Naturally composes with inline-create ("no such property → create it"), which `PropertyPicker` already has via `ConfigureNewSchemaArgs`.

Worth deciding alongside: whether `::[[Name]]` is offered at all as an authored form. It parses and late-binds today, but `core.materializePropertyChildren` canonicalizes any field row it touches to `::((fieldId))`, so the alias form is transient by design — a user who types it will see it rewritten. Either make that explicit in the UX or don't surface the form.

## 2. Property-name enforcement sits above the write seam (guard exists, wrong altitude)

`isGrammarShapedLabel` / `assertNotGrammarShapedLabel` (`src/data/referenceBlock.ts`) rejects names that are themselves reference spans — a type labelled `::((someFieldId))` would otherwise mint a block that IS a recognized property field row of the Types page. PR #436 wired it at `createTypeBlock`, `writeBlockTypeLabel`, `seedProperty`, `seedType`, and `UserSchemasService.addSchema`.

The **rename** path is the gap. `src/components/renderer/PropertySchemaBlockRenderer.tsx:118` is the only enforcement, and it is a renderer — a plugin, mutator, or the agent bridge doing `block.set(propertyNameProp, '::((id))')` bypasses it entirely. That is asymmetric with `addSchema`, which enforces the same rule in the data layer. Fix: enforce at the `propertyNameProp` write seam so every writer is covered, leaving the renderer's draft-revert as pure UX.

Two smaller items in the same area, from the §11 "Hygiene & seeds" group:
- **Definition ids must be UUID-shaped** — enforced at `addSchema`, preflight-reported for legacy rows — so `block_references` (which is UUID-scoped) is complete over field rows. Specified, not implemented.
- **Orphan-key synthesis** must reject grammar-shaped keys as a hard flip blocker. No live site yet (it's slice C flip tooling), so this is a constraint on that work rather than a change to existing code.

## 3. A refused name currently says nothing to the user

`writeBlockTypeLabel` throws a typed `GrammarShapedLabelError`; the renderer catches it, `console.error`s, and silently snaps the field back. Same shape for `addSchema` throws at `BlockProperties.tsx:214-222` / `:337-340`. On a guard that **newly rejects previously-accepted input**, silence is the wrong default — `showError` from `@/utils/toast` is already used for the type-create path in `supertags/codeMirrorExtensions.ts:137`.

title: strength-tracker: tapping before the live query resolves can start a second workout
description:
Found by the adversarial review pass on #438 (live-query lens, finding 4). Filed rather than fixed there: the fix is an adopt-or-create path that deserves its own change and tests, not an append to a data-loss batch.

## What happens

`useBlockQuery` returns an empty array while its handle is still loading, so "still loading" and "no workouts" are indistinguishable to `TonightView`. On first paint `live` is `undefined`, the write coordinator is seeded with `null`, and the surface is fully interactive — by design, since `useProgram` seeds `DEFAULT_CONFIG` synchronously so the page is usable instantly.

Tap a checkbox in that window — reload mid-session, PWA restart, phone unlock — and the coordinator sees no workout and materializes one. When the query resolves, `liveWorkouts.find(...)` adopts the *older* workout (typed-block queries order by `created_at ASC`), so the one just created is orphaned: never rendered, never finishable, excluded from history (`buildHistory` skips `in-progress`), and out of Discard's reach. It keeps a full set of pre-filled, todo-typed set blocks in the agenda forever.

The same shape can happen with two devices starting the same session simultaneously.

## Why the obvious fixes don't fit

- Blocking the UI until the queries resolve defeats the "usable the instant it mounts" property, which is the point at 1am.
- Reading `live` again before creating doesn't help: it's empty *because* the query hasn't resolved, not because there's nothing there.

## Sketch

Make the create adopt-or-create, in `store.ts`:

1. Before `materializeWorkout`, point-query for an `in-progress` workout with this `strength:date` + `strength:session`.
2. If one exists, adopt it: read its exercise/set children and return ids matched to the draft the same way `overlayLive` matches (by `strength:definition`, then by name), creating only the exercises it lacks.
3. Otherwise create as today.

That also closes the two-device start, and makes the create idempotent — worth having regardless of this trigger.

## Related

- #439 (live values vs local draft) is the same seam from the other side.

title: Fuzz pack: guard/classifier remainder (localDbCorruption, subtreeOutline)
Same-tx derivation liveness: kernel derivations can go stale when a plugin (or async path) writes their input afterward
description:
### The pattern

The same-tx processor pass is single-pass, kernel-then-plugins, no fixpoint (`commitPipeline.ts:340`). A kernel processor DERIVES state from a field; a plugin later in the same pass WRITES that field — leaving the derived state describing pre-write content. Symmetrically, an async/late-binding derivation can miss an input change that arrives via a path that never schedules it.

This isn't unique to properties-as-blocks, but PR #386 surfaced it by **adding a kernel derivation** (`reference_target_id` via `core.deriveReferenceTarget`), which retroactively obligated every content-rewriting plugin to recompute that column — and by adding the MATERIALIZE/PROJECT inverse pair, which makes a naive "just re-run the kernel" fix ping-pong.

### Full matrix (7 same-tx processors)

Kernel (in order): `typeify(properties)` → `MATERIALIZE(properties)` → `DERIVE(content)` → `PROJECT(content,referenceTargetId,parentId,orderKey,deleted)` → `NORMALIZE(references)`.
Plugins after: `alias.sync(content,properties)`, `inlineDeletedBlockRefs(content)`, `mergeRetarget(content,properties,references)`.

"Plugin writes a field a kernel processor derives from, after it ran":

| plugin write | kernel watcher | status |
|---|---|---|
| alias.sync content → DERIVE | reference_target_id | **fixed** (PR #386, inline recompute) |
| inlineDeleted content → DERIVE | reference_target_id | ok (inline recompute) |
| mergeRetarget content → DERIVE | reference_target_id | ok (inline recompute) |
| mergeRetarget references → NORMALIZE | references_json | ok (own `normalizeReferences()` call) |
| alias.sync properties → MATERIALIZE | field/value children | ok (only because `tx.setProperty` dual-writes) |
| **mergeRetarget properties → MATERIALIZE** | field/value children | **GAP** (raw `tx.update(properties)` bypasses child re-materialize) — flip-gated |
| **inlineDeleted content → PROJECT** | cell | **GAP** (a `((A))` value inlined to prose leaves the cell stale) — flip-gated |
| mergeRetarget content → PROJECT (same block) | own cell | masked (`retargetSource` patches the same block's cell too) |
| **mergeRetarget content → PROJECT (owner cell)** | owner block's cell | **GAP** (merging a property-DEFINITION block retargets its field rows `((fromDef))`→`((intoDef))` on their OWNERS; that changes which schema each owner's children denote, but the owner was projected earlier in the pass and isn't re-projected, so the owner cell stays keyed to the merged-away name) — flip-gated; raw/definition-merge only (same-named defs are already resolved by §6 shadowing, and the alias-collision merge keys on `aliasesProp` not on definition name, so no normal flow reaches this) |

Three different ad-hoc idioms already exist (recompute the stamp / call `normalizeReferences` / patch the cell). The proximate cases are fixed or flip-gated; **no live damage today.** The owner-cell variant above was originally triaged as a separate "merge × property-machinery" slice-C item during PR #386 review — it is not; it is this same derivation-liveness pattern, and the structural fix below covers it.

### Also in this family: alias-rederive scheduling gap (was areview item 7)

`repo.scheduleReferenceTargetNameRederive` (`repo.ts:2605`) has only 3 callers (`referencesProcessor.ts:487/500` for minted date/alias pages, `repo.ts:945` for sync arrivals). An alias added via the property panel / agent bridge / `alias.sync`'s own `setProperty(aliasesProp)` / `typeExtraction` never schedules the late-binding rederive, so an existing `[[Foo]]` row with a NULL stamp stays NULL until its content is next edited **or the workspace is next opened** (the per-open sweep, `scheduleWorkspaceRefBackfill` + the reference-target sweep, re-stamps everything). So staleness is bounded to "until next open," a mild trigger — not data loss.

### The structural fix (and its catch)

Re-run the kernel derive/materialize/project stage after the plugin stage, **gated by a write-generation marker** so pass two visits only rows the plugin stage touched. Naive re-run is unsafe because MATERIALIZE and PROJECT are mutual inverses (`properties → children → properties`) and would ping-pong — exactly the fixpoint the single-pass contract forbids. Kernel processors are individually idempotent (they early-return when the derived value already matches), so a correctly-scoped second pass no-ops on untouched rows. For the alias-rederive half, the principled fix is a kernel hook on "a block's alias list gained entries" rather than N per-caller `schedule` calls (which would reproduce the same forget-me failure).

### Recommendation

Follow-up, not a PR #386 blocker: proximate cases fixed, remaining gaps flip-gated with no live workspace, and the write-generation-marker design deserves its own focused pass.

title: Post-flip healing seams (slice C): recognition invalidation, background-workspace recognition, B2/materialize/restore backfills
description:
Two valid findings from the Codex review of PR #386 (properties-as-blocks slices A+B) that are deliberately NOT fixed there — both only bite **after** a workspace flips to child-backed properties, so they belong with the slice-C flip tooling. Recording them so the flip runbook/tooling design accounts for both.

## 1. Loaded children/childIds handles don't refresh when the flip arrives ([review comment](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/386#discussion_r3595677013))

`core.children` / `core.childIds` default to `VISIBLE_CHILDREN_SQL`, whose predicate reads `workspaces.properties_migration` — but the handles only declare a parent-edge dependency. A `properties_migration` change arriving via sync while the app is running invalidates nothing, so already-loaded handles keep their pre-flip visible-set until some child under that parent changes or the app reloads.

What IS covered: recognition changes driven by definition adds/renames invalidate correctly — the rows' `reference_target_id` stamps flip, and `stampReferenceTargets` / the same-tx processor fan out parent-edge invalidations.

Slice-C options: (a) flip tooling requires/prompts an app reload per client (flip is a once-per-workspace coordinated operator event, so this may be all we need); (b) a workspaces-table observer that calls a broad handle invalidation when `properties_migration` changes.

## 2. Definition renames/codec changes that sync while a workspace is inactive never trigger the B2 migration ([review comment](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/386#discussion_r3596092336))

`facetBridge` diffs `previousPropertyDefinitions` → next to schedule `schedulePropertyDefinitionMigrations` / the added-name rederive. On switching back to a workspace, prev is `null` or belongs to another workspace, so the same-workspace diff sees no changes: a rename that synced while the workspace was inactive leaves field rows titled `[[old name]]` and cells keyed by the old name until the next local touch of that definition.

Pre-flip this is moot (B2 is flip-gated; cell-era renames use the existing reprojection-marker machinery). Post-flip the durable fix is persisting a per-workspace definitions baseline (e.g. fieldId → (name, codecType) in `client_schema_state`) and diffing against it on registry prime — or folding a "field-row title/cell-key reconcile" pass into the flipped-workspace open path, mirroring the per-open `reference_target_id` sweep.

Both were called out in the PR #386 review round; fixing them there was deferred to keep the dormant-pre-flip PR converged.


---

## Wave 2 additions (Codex review of commit `7675876f`)

Three more post-flip-only findings deferred here for the same reason — all dormant while every workspace reads `cell`.

### 3. Same-tx *ancestor* content-flip nests machinery under a descendant ([review comment](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/386#discussion_r3598021081))

The write-side guards (`tx.setProperty` dual-write, the materialize processor) added a content-based `isProspectiveFieldRow` twin so a row that flips its OWN content to `[[schema]]` in the same tx as a bag write stays cell-only. But the check is self-only. If one tx changes an *ancestor's* content to a whole-block schema ref AND then writes a property bag on a *descendant*, the `isInsidePropertySubtree` walk reads the ancestor's not-yet-stamped column (derive runs later in the chain), doesn't recognize the descendant as interior, and materializes field/value rows under it; after derive stamps the ancestor those rows are interior and the visible-children rule stops filtering them, exposing machinery.

Why deferred: the trigger is an exotic single tx that both flips an ancestor's content and writes a property on a descendant — not reachable through normal UI, only raw/bridge/programmatic multi-writes. The fix threads a prospective (content-aware) predicate through the shared `isInsidePropertySubtreeWalk`, which also feeds the read-side `childrenOf` filter — a hot-path primitive change with regression surface, not worth rushing for a corner case in a dormant PR.

### 4. Foreign-workspace seed field rows can mint alias pages ([review comment](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/386#discussion_r3598021088))

`isPropertyMachineryRow` (references processor) recognizes field rows via `repo.propertySchemaResolverFor(workspaceId).resolveField(...)`, which fails **closed** for a workspace that is neither active nor previous (the registry is scoped to active/previous). A code-owned seed field-row write to such a background flipped workspace therefore isn't recognized as machinery, and its `[[seed property]]` content is parsed as a normal wikilink → a minted alias page + backlink from a hidden row. Same root cause as the derive-at-arrival cross-workspace deferral. A workspace-capable recognizer (deterministic seed-id check, or a `block_types`-based probe matching the SQL twin instead of the registry resolver) is the fix.

### 5. Refs aren't reconciled when a CAS repair turns a row into a field row ([review comment](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/386#discussion_r3598021095))

`stampReferenceTargets` (the per-open sweep + added-definition rederive) updates only the local `reference_target_id` column and fans out handle invalidations — it does not run `references.parseReferences`. So when a repair turns an existing exact `[[schema]]` child into a recognized field row, any stale `references_json` content backlink it carried from its pre-machinery life is left intact (the machinery-row suppression only runs at parse time). Fix: schedule a references reconcile for rows whose stamp transitions them into a property field target, or fold that cleanup into the repair path.

**Related (not deferred, noted):** the added-definition/rename rederive re-stamps (never *clears*) — a `[[oldName]]` row that after a rename resolves to nothing (`undefined`) keeps its stale fieldId stamp rather than clearing. Benign in practice (root rows are position-exempt; genuine field rows are retitled by the B2 pass), but the clear-to-null transition belongs with this reconcile work.

### 6. `core.restore` doesn't re-materialize property children tombstoned by a prior subtree delete ([review comment](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/386))

When a flipped-workspace block with properties is deleted, the subtree-delete paths tombstone its hidden field/value children. A later `core.restore` flips only the parent row live and usually leaves its `properties` bag unchanged; because `MATERIALIZE_PROPERTY_CHILDREN_PROCESSOR` watches `properties`, the restore doesn't re-materialize the missing children, so the restored block keeps its local cell value but loses the child-backed truth sync/projection relies on.

Note: an undo of the subtree delete restores the whole subtree (children included) via replay, so this bites only a standalone `core.restore` on the parent alone. Fix belongs with the flip tooling / a restore→re-materialize seam. Dormant pre-flip.

_(Separately, the wave-2 "projection collection ancestry" observation — `collectAffectedProjection` treating a ref-typed value as a field row — is already handled at HEAD: `reprojectParentField` guards with `isInsidePropertySubtree(parent.id)`, so an over-collected value whose parent is a field row returns early. It was valid only against the intermediate commit it reviewed.)_

### 7. SQL and the tx-layer recognizer disagree on not-yet-materialized SEED definitions (moved from #404 item 7)

Moved out of #404 because it is not a pre-flip correctness item: it is dormant until a workspace is child-backed, and it is a hole in the **invisibility half** that gates the slice-C flip (§11) — the blanket hide that keeps C's backfill from dumping raw `((fieldId))` rows into production outlines before slice D's tree UI exists.

**Divergence.** `VISIBLE_CHILD_PREDICATE_SQL` (`treeQueries.ts`) answers "is this child's `reference_target_id` a property definition?" from the `block_types` side index, which only carries definition blocks that exist in `blocks`. The tx-layer checker (`txEngine.isFieldDefinitionCheckerFor` → the registry) *also* recognizes code-declared property seeds that `materializePropertySeeds` hasn't written yet. Same row, two answers: hidden by an in-tx read, shown by the reactive query.

**Two windows, not one.** Boot before seeds materialize — closed operationally by the slice-C runbook (materialize before any flip). *And* a field row arriving over sync ahead of its definition block, which no boot-time ordering rule covers, on an already-warm device. The second window is what makes this worth fixing rather than documenting.

**Scope — only the seed half is a divergence.**
- **Seed definitions:** the registry knows them regardless of materialization or arrival, so both windows close by giving the predicate the same registry-derived knowledge. This is the item.
- **User-authored definitions:** neither side knows them until the block arrives, so both answer "not a definition" — consistent and self-healing, a transient mis-render rather than a divergence. Not in scope; no machinery warranted.

**Proposed fix — same shape as item 4's "deterministic seed-id check".** Property seed definition ids are deterministic (`propertyDefinitionBlockId(workspaceId, seedKey)` = `uuidv5("${workspaceId}:${seedKey}", DEFINITION_SEED_NS)`), so the set is computable in JS from the registry with no DB read. Bind it into the predicate (a JSON array + `json_each`, one extra param) rather than storing it: no new table, nothing to invalidate, `block_types` keeps its trigger-derived-from-`blocks` invariant, and a newly loaded plugin's seeds are known on the next query. Verify the visible-children query-build path can reach the registry; if not, fall back to a small local seed-id index. Can land with C's invisibility half — it does not need to wait for slice D.

**Do NOT converge the other direction.** Making the tx layer forget seeds is not an option: the same checker is the write-side positional gate (`txEngine.isInsidePropertySubtree`, `isProspectiveFieldRow`), where under-recognizing lets the `setProperty` dual-write nest machinery under a field row or property-subtree interior — structure recognition can never reclaim, written into synced `blocks` data.

**Interaction with slice D.** D retargets the predicate at the *hidden-tier* set ("is this a hidden-tier definition?" rather than "is this a definition?"), which is also registry-derived — so D wants this same mechanism and should reuse it, not replace it.


### 8. A rename migration can delete a *different* definition's rows when it unshadows them ([review comment](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/386#discussion_r3612542549))

Codex P2, confirmed by tracing the code (not inferred from comments). Two definitions **A** and **B** share the name `status`; A wins on `(createdAt, fieldId)` sort, B is shadowed.

**Why B gets no plan.** `changedPropertyDefinitions` (`propertyDefinitionMigrations.ts:60-86`) diffs each fieldId against *its own* previous name/codec and `continue`s when neither changed (`:77`). It never consults winner status. When A renames away, the registry rebuild re-groups B as the sole — hence winning — entry for `status` (`propertyDefinitionRegistry.ts:130-138`), but B's own metadata is untouched, so no plan is emitted for it. Milder symptom on its own: B's existing field/value children stay out of the parent cell until some later child edit.

**Why it escalates to deletion.** A's own migration rewrites the shared parent's cell in one `tx.update(parent.id, {properties})` (`repo.ts:2978`), dropping `status` and adding the new name. That fires `MATERIALIZE_PROPERTY_CHILDREN_PROCESSOR` in the same tx. For `status`, `resolveNameSchema` now resolves to **B** (the new winner), so `matchingChildren` are B's rows — and because the cell key is gone, it takes the delete branch:

```
286  if (encoded === undefined) {
       // "Key removed from the cell by a LOCAL write: the delete is the user's intent"
291    for (const child of matchingChildren) await deleteSubtreeInTx(tx, child.id)
```

That comment is the broken assumption: the key was removed by **A's rename migration**, not by a user deleting the property, so "user intent" doesn't hold — and B's rows, unrelated to A, are tombstoned.

**Severity.** Soft-delete, so recoverable from history rather than lost. Flip-gated dormant (`isPropertyChildBackedWorkspace` at `propertyChildrenProcessor.ts:444`; `readIsChildBackedWorkspace` at `repo.ts:2754`). Additional precondition for the deletion half: B must already have field/value children on the *same parent* that carries A's — plausible via sync from another device or a duplicate-definition typo, which is the premise the report starts from. Without that, only the milder unprojected-until-next-edit symptom applies.

**Fix direction (undecided).** Two candidates, and they are not equivalent:
1. Treat **winner-status changes** as migration/reprojection triggers, not just name/codec diffs — what the reviewer proposed. Correct but widens the diff's contract.
2. Narrow the materialize processor's "absent key = user intent" inference so a **migration-authored** cell rewrite isn't read as a user deletion. Smaller, and arguably fixes the actual wrong assumption rather than compensating for it downstream.

Worth deciding deliberately rather than in a review-response pass; (2) looks closer to the root cause.

**No existing coverage:** `propertyDefinitionMigrations.test.ts`'s "simultaneous name swap" (`:317-391`) is a different shape — two distinct never-shadowed names, both fieldIds already in `plans`. No test combines shadowing with the migration/materialize pipeline.

title: Alias release-reclaim leaves old wikilink bindings on the tombstoned ex-claimant
description:
Found by the references fuzzer's new stable-wrong-binding sweep (PR for issue #372 Batch 3). Sibling of #378 (restore-side stale claims) — this is the binding side of the same alias-ownership-lifecycle gap.

## Repro shape (minimized by fast-check)

1. Block X writes `[[ax]]` → no claimant → alias seat S is minted and claims `ax`; X's binding → S.
2. S is **deleted** → its `block_aliases` row is gone (the index is live-only), so `ax` is unclaimed. X's stored binding still points at tombstoned S — deliberately retained by the add-only/reconcile contract, so restoring S rebinds cleanly.
3. Another block (e.g. ROOT) sets `alias: ['ax']` → **succeeds** (no live claimant, no uniqueness conflict).
4. Nothing revisits X: `parseReferences` fires only on X's own row changes, `renameProcessor` only on *removed* aliases of a live block, `mergeRetarget` only on merges. X's `[[ax]]` stays bound to the tombstone forever while every *fresh* `[[ax]]` binds to ROOT — same mark text, permanently different targets by write time.

Deterministic replay: `FUZZ_SEED=1545608434 FUZZ_PATH="34:3:2:4:4:4:6:7:8:8:9:11:12:15:15:18:17:17:16:18:9:27:24:26:26:26:26:12:19:19:17:17:17:17:17:17" FUZZ_RUNS=1 yarn vitest run src/plugins/references/test/referencesRecompute.fuzz.test.ts -t 'fixpoint'` (against the sweep WITHOUT its live-bound scoping — the committed sweep deliberately skips tombstone-bound entries and cites this issue).

## Why it needs a design decision, not a quick fix

- Retargeting tombstone-bound entries at claim time would break undo/restore of the old claimant (the retained binding is what makes restore rebind cleanly), and a restore AFTER a retarget hits #378's collision problem in reverse.
- Blocking the new claim while tombstone-bound refs exist punishes a legitimate rename/recreate flow.
- A "claim-watch" processor (on alias gained: rewrite tombstone-bound `[[alias]]` sources to the new claimant) is the eager option, but it must decide what a later restore of the old target means.

The fuzz sweep now polices only the LIVE-bound invariant (two live blocks must never disagree about an alias — the class behind PR #371's bug #20 and this branch's date-literal fix); tombstone-bound residuals are documented as unpoliced pending this decision.

title: Raw tx.restore call sites can resurrect a tombstone's stale alias claim (getOrCreateDailyNote, Journal, kernelPage)
description:
Split out of PR #371's adversarial review (round 2, verified by repro).

PR #371 fixed the stale-claim-resurrection class inside `createOrRestoreTargetBlock` (opt-in `stripAliasesOnRestore`, used by the alias/daily seat wrappers). The same shape exists at raw `tx.restore` call sites that re-claim the tombstone's alias bag as-is — the `blocks_alias_update` trigger re-inserts the bag's aliases on the `deleted` flip and trips uniqueness **in the restore statement**:

- `src/plugins/daily-notes/dailyNotes.ts` `getOrCreateDailyNote` restore branch — repro'd: create a daily note → delete it → another page claims the freed date alias → navigate to that day → `ProcessorRejection: alias.collision`; the day is persistently unopenable until the user un-aliases the claimant.
- `getOrCreateJournalBlock` restore branch (alias `Journal`) — same shape.
- `src/data/kernelPage.ts` restore path — same shape.

A bag-strip alone does NOT fully fix these entry points: their follow-up `setProperty(aliases, …)` (and the live-row `needsRepair` repair path) still unconditionally claim the aliases and would collide with the squatter. Needs a domain decision for the squatted-alias case: bind to the claimant / skip the contested alias / surface the existing alias-collision-merge flow.

Related residual noted in the same review (documented, self-healing, low priority): plain lookup-resolved bindings in `parseReferences` get no write-phase recheck, so a claimant renamed in the milliseconds between plan build and apply can leave a stale binding if the rename processor's concurrent pass reads `block_references` before the parse write commits; heals on the next edit of the source.

title: Seed revision upgrades: operator step to refresh materialized mirrors, then safe automation
description:
## Summary

When a code-declared property **seed bumps its `revision`** (changing preset / config / default / changeScope), the **materialized definition row** — the per-workspace mirror — is **not** refreshed automatically. Behavior is already correct on clients that have the declaration (code is authoritative: the registry never reads a seeded row's behavioral fields where a declaration is present), but the stored bag stays at the old revision until an explicit operator step rewrites it.

This tracks (1) building that operator step, and (2) eventually automating it **safely**.

## Current state

- `materializePropertySeeds` (`src/data/definitionSeeds.ts`) is **create/restore-only** and explicitly *does not repair payloads*. On a revision mismatch it only logs:
  > `[definitionSeeds] <seedKey> revision N trails code revision M; background materialization does not repair payloads`
- So a revision bump takes effect for code-having clients immediately (one-source rule), but the stale mirror is still read by **plugin-less clients' fallback builds** and by **inspection / the property panel**.
- The tx-layer guard (`SeededDefinitionWriteError`) blocks *user-scope* (`BlockDefault`) writes to seed definition bags but **allows `Automation`-scope** writes — which is exactly the write path an upgrade step would use.

## Why it isn't automatic today (design rationale — schema-unification §4.3 / §6 / §13)

Automatic background reconciliation would be a **PATCH-class write decided from local state**, which is unsafe here:

- `revision` lives inside the opaque/encrypted `properties_json` bag, so the server can't compare-and-set on it — sync is plain last-writer-wins on the column.
- A client whose replica is stale / partially-downloaded could "repair" the row and **win the LWW, rolling the fleet back** (local at N, another client already pushed N+1, "repair to N" clobbers N+1).
- Making it safe requires a **download-drain / checkpoint primitive** ("a full checkpoint completed after this workspace's buckets joined the subscription set" — `SyncStatus.statusForPriority` / `lastSyncedAt`, **not** `onFirstSync`'s client-global `hasSynced`), which v1 deferred (the properties-as-blocks work #288 needs the same primitive).
- v1 sidesteps the whole PATCH-from-local-state class: the background pass is create-only; upgrades are explicit post-sync operator steps.

Because the one-source rule makes a stale mirror invisible to behavior where code is present, this is **low-urgency** — but plugin-less clients and inspection do read the stale bag, so it shouldn't be ignored forever.

## Proposed work

**Phase 1 — the operator step (near-term).** A deliberate, run-once-after-sync-complete action that rewrites a seed's materialized row to `canonicalPropertySeedProperties(seed)` at the new revision:
- runs under **Automation** scope (whole-bag `tx.update`, allowed by the guard);
- preserves `created_at` (winner ordering) — a whole-bag `update` already does;
- touches one row → syncs to the fleet as an ordinary update (no fleet data-migration);
- surfaced as a CLI / agent-bridge verb (e.g. `upgrade-seed <seedKey>` / upgrade-all-drifted), driven by the drift the pass already logs.

**Phase 2 — safe automation (eventual).** Gate an automatic upgrade pass behind the checkpoint/drain primitive so a PATCH decision is never made against a partial replica, then repair drift in the background. Overlaps with #288 (same primitive).

## Constraints / invariants
- Never PATCH a seed row from local state without a completeness signal (fleet-rollback vector above).
- `Automation` scope only — `BlockDefault` is user-owned and blocked by the tx guard.
- Preserve `created_at`.
- Whole-bag canonical rewrite keyed by `revision`.

## References
- Design: `docs/schema-unification.html` §4.3 ("No drain-hold"), §6 (reconciliation / "no revision guard"), §13 (rollout runbook).
- Code: `src/data/definitionSeeds.ts` (`materializePropertySeeds`, the drift log); the tx guard `SeededDefinitionWriteError` + its `Automation` exemption.
- Related: #288 (properties-as-blocks migration — supplies the checkpoint/drain primitive), #370 (workspace isolation).
- Surfaced during PR #364 (schema unification slice B).

title: Fuzzing roadmap: remaining targets (sync, e2ee, materialization, interactions)
description:
Follow-up to the fuzzing infrastructure in #371 (harness in `src/test/fuzz.ts`, tiers + conventions in `docs/fuzzing.md`). This is the map of remaining fuzz targets from a code-grounded exploration of four areas: sync, encryption, materialization, and user interactions. Each item lists target, oracle, and effort so suites can be picked off independently.

## Batch 1 — pure/cheap, smoke-tier friendly *(in progress on the #371 branch)*

- [ ] **Crypto codecs + envelopes + AAD injectivity** (`src/sync/crypto/`): decode∘encode == identity for base64url/base32/hex, `enc:v1:` (`envelope.ts`) and `encb:v1:` (`binaryEnvelope.ts`) envelopes, `parseWorkspaceKey`/`formatWorkspaceKey`, `digestFromContentHash`/`computeContentHash`; decode of arbitrary garbage throws only the module's typed `Error`, never TypeError/RangeError; AAD length-prefix injectivity (`aad.ts` — `["A","BC"]` must not alias `["AB","C"]`; contentAad/assetBytesAad/canaryAad disjointness). Pure, sync, no WebCrypto.
- [ ] **`decideStagingRow` LWW model** (`src/data/internals/syncObserver/reconcile.ts:71`): fuzz event sequences (materializability × pendingUpload × remote stamps produced by a model of the server monotonic clamp — `greatest(old,new)` + content-change bump, per `supabase/migrations/20260612000000_add_user_updated_at_monotonic_clamp.sql`). Oracles: totality; `defer` ⟺ materializability defer; pending ⟹ skip-stale; equal-nonzero-stamp idempotence (I1) / stamp-0 exemption (I2); convergence — the gate applies the highest stamp then holds.
- [ ] **Upload-queue algebra** (`src/services/powersync.ts`, via the exported `__…ForTest` hooks): `compactBlockCrudEntries` — replaying compacted ops yields the same final per-id state as replaying raw entries; same-tx PATCH fuses into create (the preference-wipe guard); DELETE cancels prior ops; first-appearance order preserved. `orderedBlockUpserts` — output is a permutation, parents-first for in-batch parents, terminates on cycles.
- [ ] **Paste planners** (`src/paste/operations.ts`): `planSingleBlockPaste` — cursor == from + insert.length, CRLF/CR normalization; `planEditModeMultilinePaste` — from/to clamped to `[0, currentContent.length]`, `focusOffsetInTarget` within `targetContent`, fenced-code root keeps full body; never throws.
- [ ] **`orderKeyPlacement`** (`src/data/orderKeyPlacement.ts`): fake-Tx harness recording `move` calls; random sibling arrays with deliberate orderKey ties; final (orderKey, id) ordering places n new keys exactly adjacent to the anchor with no ties (the #198/#182/#188 tie-collision area).
- [ ] **Trigger-index mirror sweeps in the stateful fuzzer** (`src/data/test/repoMutators.fuzz.test.ts`): `block_aliases` == `$.alias` of live blocks, `block_types` == `$.types`, `blocks_fts` (via `blocks_fts_rowids`) == live non-empty content, no orphan rowids — none of these trigger-maintained indexes has any consistency check today, not even in the audit. Also fix the **vacuous `references_index_mirror` sweep**: the audit runs in the fuzzer, but the op set never writes `references_json` and the kernel-only test repo doesn't register the references plugin, so the mirror check passes trivially — add ops that write references so it bites.

## Batch 2 — medium effort

- [x] **References recompute oracle** (highest-severity class — this is the "~10k SRS backlinks stripped" incident shape): register the references/alias plugins in the fuzz repo (`createTestRepo({extensions})`), generate content with `[[alias]]`/`((uuid))` marks + ref-typed properties, assert `references_json` == from-scratch recompute via the audit's full checks (`content_link_recompute` at `src/plugins/data-integrity/audit.ts:496`, `property_ref_projection` at `:375`).
- [x] **AEAD round-trip + tamper rejection** (`src/sync/crypto/aead.ts`, `byteAead.ts`): `open(k, seal(k, x, aad), aad) == x` for arbitrary UTF-8/bytes; any single-byte payload flip or AAD field swap (block/workspace/column) rejects — never wrong plaintext; `validateCanary` returns false and never throws on arbitrary wrong keys/canaries. WebCrypto works in plain node vitest; `fc.asyncProperty` + the `keyFrom(fill)` deterministic-key idiom.
- [x] **Query-handle soundness** (`src/data/internals/handleStore.ts`): subscribe a pool of `repo.query.*` handles over random args, run random mutator ops, assert every `handle.peek()` deep-equals a fresh `.load()` of the same query — catches missed `ctx.depend(...)` in resolvers (stale-UI class). Probe pattern in `kernelQueries.test.ts`.
- [x] **Split/merge content conservation** (interaction level): split at random offset then merge back == identity; total pre-order text conserved across any split; tree validity + undo round-trip after each command. Pure at the `repo.mutate.split`/`merge` boundary — no EditorView needed.
- [x] **Interaction action-sequence fuzzer**: dispatch random `EDIT_MODE_CM`/`NORMAL_MODE`/`MULTI_SELECT_MODE` actions through `invokeAction` (`src/shortcuts/actionDispatch.ts:46`) against a test repo, deps synthesized from a headless `EditorState`-backed fake editorView (handlers only read `state.selection.main`/`state.doc` and call `dispatch`). Reuse the full `repoMutators.fuzz` oracle set + undo-all/redo-all. Exclude the four layout-bound `move_*_from_cm_*` arrow actions (visual-line geometry is browser-only).
- [x] **Selection state machine** (`src/utils/selection.ts`): pure parts (`blockIdsInOrderedSelectionRange`, `findBestSelectionAnchorIndex`) — contiguous visible-order ranges, toggle-twice identity; `validateSelectionHierarchy` never yields a parent+descendant pair.

**Batch 2 status (2026-07-14, PR #371):** all six suites landed. The references-pipeline fuzzer found and fixed FOUR real bugs on day one (restore didn't re-derive refs for tombstone-edited content; `[[date]]` colliding with an existing date-alias owner permanently failed the processor tx; merge retargeted property-ref entries without the property value; a stale parse plan could clobber the rename rewriter's concurrent update). The interaction fuzzer found a fifth: `delete_block` was the only structural handler with no scope-root guard (fixed via `StructuralEditPolicy.canDelete`). Details in `docs/fuzzing.md` "Found so far".

## Batch 3 — heavy scaffolding, decide after Batch 2

- [ ] **Stateful materialization fuzz** (`src/data/internals/syncObserver/materialize.ts:261`): random staging writes / pending uploads / flushes through `setupObserverTestDb` (`syncObserver/test/harness.ts`); differential against pure `decideStagingRow`; incremental drains == from-scratch materialize of the terminal staging set; quarantine never wedges the batch; queue drains to 0.
- [ ] **Two-repo convergence fuzzer**: interleaved mutator sequences on repo A and repo B with random sync points; after a final bidirectional flush both `blocks` tables are byte-identical + all structural sweeps pass. **Blocker:** needs a JS fake server implementing the monotonic clamp + `ps_crud` → `blocks_synced` threading (no such component exists — today's tests hand-write staging rows). Two repos over one infra need distinct `newId`/`now` (`createTestRepo.ts` caveats). Most new scaffolding, highest coverage — also unlocks true multi-device conflict fuzzing.

## Explicitly out of scope for fast-check

Visual-line / caret-geometry navigation (`isOnFirstVisualLine`, `getCaretRect`, `placeCursorAtX` in `src/utils/codemirror.ts`) — needs a real browser layout engine; belongs to Playwright/e2e.

## Conventions

Every suite follows `docs/fuzzing.md`: line-1 `// @vitest-environment node`, `fuzzParams(N)` sized so the file's smoke tier stays ≲1s, code-cited oracles, oracle discipline (never weaken a failing property — diagnose real-bug vs wrong-oracle first), nondeterminism pinned (seeded LCG over `Math.random`, deterministic keys, injected clocks).

title: Workspace isolation: cross-workspace bleed via globally-visible contributions + hard-error foreign resolution (captured-registry end-state)
description:
Property definitions can **bleed across workspaces**: contributions are visible in workspace registries they don't belong to, and the resolver trusts code-owned handles for a workspace it doesn't have loaded ("foreign"). This tracks tightening that toward real per-workspace isolation.

## Concrete trigger: dynamic-extension seeds

A dynamic extension (user code living in an extension **block**) declares a property seed; at load time `bindExtensionPropertySeed` (`src/extensions/dynamicExtensions.ts`) rewrites its key to `<blockId>/property/<key>` and contributes it as an **ordinary static, non-workspace-scoped** contribution — so it lands in the property registry *regardless of which workspace's registry is being built*. In principle, while workspace A is active, A's extension property could resolve/write on a block in workspace B that never installed that extension — the cross-workspace bleed the isolation design exists to prevent.

**Largely mitigated already:** the app runtime is rebuilt **per-workspace** on switch (`AppRuntimeProvider` re-resolves with `dynamicExtensionsExtension({workspaceId})`; the loader reads only the new workspace's blocks, `dynamicExtensions.ts:186`). So once you're *in* B, A's extensions aren't in B's runtime — no bleed. The residual is a **B block resolved while A is still active** (no switch yet): A's runtime carries A's extension seed and the resolver trusts plugin-origin handles cross-workspace.

## The generalization

Dynamic extensions end up workspace-scoped by the runtime rebuild. **Static (kernel + plugin) contributions are still global** — visible in every workspace's registry. Open design question: *should static plugin (and possibly kernel) contributions be workspace-scoped too?* "Static contributions being global kinda doesn't make sense" for an isolation model.

## Two sides

### 1. Registry-visibility — *what's in a workspace's registry*
- Dynamic-extension seeds: effectively scoped by the per-workspace runtime rebuild.
- Static **plugin** contributions: currently global — candidate for workspace-scoping.
- **Kernel** contributions: currently global — see the punted decision below.

### 2. Resolution — *what the resolver does for a block whose workspace isn't loaded ("foreign")*
The resolver is keyed by the **block's own workspace** (`propertySchemaResolverFor(data.workspaceId)`). When that workspace is neither active nor the one-deep retained one, it's "foreign." Three tiers:
- **Current — handle-trust (pragmatic bridge, on the branch):** kernel handles resolve; plugin handles resolve with a decode-fallback; plain schemas fail closed. Not incorrect — it keeps legitimate in-flight kernel writes working (below).
- **Plugin-only tightening (small win):** additionally fail *plugin* handles closed for foreign. Breaks only `mediaCapture`'s parameterized `{workspaceId: WS2}` and #186's daily-note (both retain-covered or non-existent in production) plus the resolver boundary tests. Kernel keeps resolving.
- **Captured-registry refactor (true end-state):** make foreign resolution a **hard error**, and have legitimate cross-workspace ops carry their own resolver so they never hit the foreign path.

## Why foreign *kernel* resolution exists today — don't naively fail-close it

Reject-even-kernel was tried in #364 and **refuted**: it broke 3 navigation tests that are *not* artifacts. `navigate` captures its originating workspace up front; an async step (confirm dialog / observer) flips the active workspace; the navigation then writes **kernel ui-state** (`topLevelBlockId`/`scrollTop`/`focusedBlockLocation`, all `system:kernel-data` seeds, `panelHistory.ts:225-230`) to its **originating** (now two-back / "foreign") workspace. Kernel schemas are workspace-**independent**, so that write is *correct*. A block always has a fixed `workspaceId` and a write always targets its **own** workspace; the only variable is whether that equals the active workspace at write time. So any tightening must either keep kernel resolving **or** give these ops a captured resolver.

## Captured-registry design sketch (the end-state)

"Pass it around." At an operation's start, capture a resolver bound to the **target** workspace — `repo.propertySchemaResolverFor(targetWs)` (or its registry snapshot) — and thread that captured resolver into the deferred write (via tx options or a closure). The write then resolves against the workspace it was **initiated for**, not whatever is active/retained when it lands. This makes retain-depth (N) irrelevant — an op can never outrun the window, however deep — and lets the base resolver treat foreign as a **hard error**. (Alternative, `navigate`-specific: switch active *first*.)

## ⚠️ Open decision (PUNTED): full isolation vs. kernel-global

Kernel-global is the *current* design (workspace-independent identity), and the pragmatic bridge relies on it. But **full isolation** — where *nothing* resolves for a foreign workspace, kernel included, and every legitimate cross-workspace op carries a captured resolver — is on the table and is the current lean. **Deferred; decide when we pick this up.** The captured-registry refactor is a prerequisite for the full-isolation option (it's what keeps the legit ops working once kernel stops resolving foreign). Do **not** treat "kernel stays global" as settled.

## What shipped in #364 (context, not this issue)
- **ref-backfill active-gate** (`c7cb626`) — a deferred batch reprojection now skips a workspace that's no longer active (operation-level gating; the right shape for deferred jobs).
- **Handle-trust kept** — the reject-even-kernel flip was reverted.

## Proposed work
- [ ] Decide **full-isolation vs kernel-global** (currently punted; leaning full isolation).
- [ ] Registry-visibility: workspace-scope static **plugin** contributions (dynamic extensions already effectively scoped); decide whether kernel contributions scope or stay global.
- [ ] Implement the **captured-registry** refactor so legitimate cross-workspace ops (navigation intent-seam, srs reschedule, `captureMedia`/daily-notes `{workspaceId}` ops) carry a resolver captured at call time.
- [ ] Once captured-registry lands, tighten the base resolver toward the chosen stance (plugin-only, or full hard-error).
- [ ] Restructure tests that model non-production foreign flows to honest ones (`mediaCapture` → `setActiveWorkspaceId(WS2)` before the second capture; srs #186 → confirm retain covers the active-at-tx-start flow).
- [ ] Correct the resolver comments (`propertySchemaResolution.ts:125`, `repo.ts:591`) that overstate current behavior as "fails closed."

## Pointers / related
- `src/extensions/dynamicExtensions.ts` — `bindExtensionPropertySeed` (the static, non-scoped contribution).
- `src/data/internals/propertySchemaResolution.ts` — `HandleTrustingPropertySchemaResolver` (kernel resolve / plugin decode-fallback / plain fail-closed).
- `src/data/repo.ts` — `registryForWorkspace` (one-deep retain), `propertySchemaResolverFor`.
- #364 — reject-even-kernel attempt (reverted) + ref-backfill gate (`c7cb626`).
- #186 — "don't touch un-open workspaces" rule (cross-workspace undo; fixed). #226 — read-only flag lags active-workspace switch.

*(Reframed from the original "operation-level gating" framing, which was a different isolation angle. The real thread is globally-visible contributions + hard-error foreign resolution via captured-registry.)*

title: Investigate iPad Safari normal-mode block copy failures
description:
## Problem
Normal-mode block copy appears unreliable on iPad Safari when triggered from hardware-key shortcuts. The affected actions include the focused-block copy path and selected-block copy path.

## Relevant code paths
- src/shortcuts/blockActions.ts defines the normal-mode copy action with +c and y y bindings.
- src/shortcuts/defaultShortcuts.ts defines multi-select copy with +c and y bindings.
- src/utils/copy.ts serializes block subtrees and writes via navigator.clipboard.write with ClipboardItem.
- Several simpler reference/content copy actions use navigator.clipboard.writeText instead.

## Investigation scope
- Reproduce on iPad Safari with a hardware keyboard in normal mode.
- Determine whether shortcut matching, preventDefault timing, ClipboardItem support, clipboard permission/user-activation behavior, or selection state is the failing layer.
- Decide whether subtree copy should fall back to writeText when ClipboardItem or navigator.clipboard.write is unavailable or rejected.
- Add focused coverage for the chosen behavior, including the selected-block path if it shares the same clipboard writer.

title: Record originating client/build metadata for synced writes
description:
## Context

During the Matrix prefs investigation, the local DB showed the destructive event as `source = sync` with `tx_id = null`. That proves the connected client received the write from sync, but it does not identify which client, browser origin/profile, app build, or extension version produced the bad upload.

## Problem

For replicated/background writes, the current local event trail answers "not this client" but not "which client/build did this." That makes cross-device sync bugs hard to attribute, especially when a stale local row or preview build writes a full `properties_json` payload.

## Proposal

Add non-secret origin metadata to uploaded command/write batches and preserve it in local diagnostics after sync materialization.

Useful fields could include:

- stable per-install/client id
- browser/profile/origin identifier where available
- app build id/version/git SHA
- extension source block id and source hash for extension-authored writes, where applicable
- bridge/profile id for agent-authored writes, where applicable
- upload timestamp / local tx id correlation that survives through server echo

## Acceptance criteria

- A future `row_events.source = sync` record can be traced to an origin client/build without reading local secret stores.
- Metadata is available in diagnostics/SQL for investigations, but does not expose tokens, localStorage secrets, or user content beyond existing event snapshots.
- The implementation covers normal app writes, plugin/effect writes, and agent bridge writes.
- Tests verify metadata is attached on upload and visible after sync materialization.

## Notes

This is observability/debuggability work. It would not have prevented the Matrix prefs clobber, but it would have made the responsible client/build much easier to identify.

title: Gate mutating plugin effects until initial workspace sync is ready
description:
## Context

The Matrix prefs incident showed a race where an enabled extension/effect can run against a locally incomplete deterministic prefs row. A token-less or not-yet-synced client wrote `matrix:status = unconfigured`; because `properties_json` uploads are column-level, that stale local property map propagated and removed sibling Matrix config keys.

This issue tracks the runtime/sync-readiness layer. It is not a replacement for fixing property-level clobbering or for making Matrix status device-local.

## Problem

Plugin/app effects currently have no way to say "I mutate durable workspace/user state and should not start until initial sync/materialization has caught up." If the extension source and enabled intent arrive before dependent config/state rows, the effect can write defaults or status into partially materialized rows.

## Proposal

Add an effect-level readiness contract for mutating/background effects, for example:

- immediate effects may continue to start at runtime construction time
- mutating/background effects can declare they require workspace sync/materialization readiness
- the runtime defers those effects until the active workspace has drained initial `blocks_synced` materialization, or until an explicit offline/no-sync policy says it is safe to proceed
- deferred effects should still clean up correctly across reloads, workspace switches, safe mode, and extension enable/disable changes

## Acceptance criteria

- There is a documented API/convention for effect readiness.
- Existing effects that write durable prefs/config/checkpoints can opt into the readiness gate.
- The gate has deterministic tests for a plugin effect that would otherwise write before its prefs block/config row arrives.
- The implementation does not block purely presentational extensions or settings UI from rendering.

## Notes

This narrows the startup race window. It does not solve stale full-map `properties_json` overwrites by itself; that needs a separate property-write intent fix.

title: Video notes view is a modal overlay, not navigation — make it a pane-scoped, URL-addressable view mode
description:
## Problem

The video player's notes view (video left, editable child notes right — hover button or `$mod+Shift+n`) is a **modal takeover rather than a place you navigate to**:

- It renders as a viewport-fixed overlay (`fixed inset-0 z-50`, `src/plugins/video-player/VideoPlayerRenderer.tsx`) painted over the header and every other pane, regardless of which pane the video lives in.
- It's driven by `video:playerView`, a `ChangeScope.UiState` property **on the video block itself** (`view.ts`). Consequences:
  - **Invisible to navigation.** The hash ↔ panel-layout projection never sees it: entering/leaving notes view pushes no history entry, so browser Back while in notes view navigates the layout *underneath* the overlay instead of exiting the view.
  - **Layout round-trips destroy it.** `LayoutSlot`s encode only *which block* a pane shows, never *how* — so anything that reconciles panel rows (switching to another saved layout and back, following a link and pressing Back, session restore) loses/mistimes the view, and the pane remount tears down the `<video>`: playback stops and the position is lost.
  - **Wrong scope.** UiState syncs, so toggling notes view on one device flips it for that block on every device and in every pane.

Expected instead: a **pane-scoped view mode that participates in navigation** — Back exits it, Forward re-enters, layout snapshots (session restore, saved layouts, shared URLs) reproduce it exactly, and returning to it doesn't lose playback (ideally the video is still playing).

## Proposed approach

Full design doc (file pointers, alternatives, test plan): https://github.com/spolakh/knowledge-medium/blob/master/docs/video-notes-navigation-native.md — happy to adjust and follow up with a PR.

**1. Pane view mode in the layout substrate (small, generic core change).** A new `panel:viewMode` property on panel rows (UiState, same family as `topLevelBlockIdProp`) — an opaque plugin-owned mode id, unset = default. Extend the leaf slot grammar to carry it: `#ws/a/b~video-notes/c` (`~` is safe; ids are UUIDs, reserved chars today are `/ ( ) : ,`). Thread it through `parseSlot`/`buildLayoutSlot`, `layoutSlotsFromRows`, `sameLayoutSlots` (a mode change *is* a layout change), and `reconcilePanelRows` — reusing the existing row on a mode-only diff so the panel id (focus, scroll, panel history, React subtree) stays stable. History, Back/Forward, session restore, and layout-serializing extensions then all work via the existing projection machinery — no new sync or storage concepts.

**2. Video plugin rides on it.** `VideoPlayerLayout` gates on the *panel's* mode (when the video is the pane's top-level block) instead of the block prop; enter/exit paths write the panel prop; `video:playerView` is retired (stale values are ignorable dead UiState data). Presentation becomes a **pane takeover (`absolute inset-0`) rather than viewport takeover** — with one pane it looks the same minus the covered header; with splits, other panes stay usable. (Deliberate behavior change — flagging for discussion; a "maximize pane" affordance could follow separately.)

**3. Playback continuity, two stages.**
- **Stage A (ships with the change):** an in-memory `Map<blockId, {currentTime, playing}>` in the plugin; record on pause/seek/unmount, seek + resume on remount. Makes Back/Forward and layout round-trips lossless up to a brief remount gap. No UiState writes (high-frequency, device-local).
- **Stage B (follow-up):** a parked-player host mounted once at app level (same seam as `DialogHost`): stable container divs per active video, `ReactPlayer` portaled into them exactly once, panes *adopt* the container DOM (`moveBefore()` where available, `appendChild` fallback) and return it on unmount — so the video keeps playing while its pane is away. Bounded retention (keep only playing videos + short grace, cap N, evict → Stage A). This is the only part with platform risk, hence separated.

## Alternatives considered (rejected)

- **Hash query param** — `sameLayoutSlots` ignores params, so reconciliation/history wouldn't fire without special-casing; panel ids in shared URLs are meaningless elsewhere.
- **Keep the block prop + manual pushState shim** — fights the projection's ownership of the hash; still invisible to layout serialization; still block-global.
- **`rendererProp` override** — document-scoped/undoable/synced; can't express "only in this pane".
- **React `<Activity>` around panes** — layout switches *delete* panel rows, so you'd have to keep every historical layout mounted; parked-player host scopes retention to the one expensive resource.

## Open questions

1. Opaque mode string vs. a `panelViewModesFacet` registry (validate/drop unknown modes at reconcile)?
2. Separator char: `~` vs `!` vs `.`?
3. Should `panelHistory`'s `VisitState` also capture the mode so in-panel chevrons restore it (it's declared extensible)? Proposed: yes, if cheap.

title: Layout dead-ends: closing the last pane leaves an unrecoverable empty workspace; an active pane on a missing block strands keyboard nav
description:
Found while building layout-driving extensions downstream (spolakh fork). Three related ways the panel layout reaches a state where the app *looks* alive but keyboard navigation is dead, with no runtime recovery. All verified against current `master` (`ec49e85b`); line numbers from there. Repro recipes at the bottom were confirmed in a live tab.

## 1. Closing the last pane leaves an unrecoverable empty workspace

`close_current_panel` (`src/shortcuts/defaultShortcuts.ts:304-312`) calls `deletePanelRow` with no last-pane guard. For the last top-level row, `nextActivePanelAfterClose` walks to the layout session, finds no sibling, and returns `undefined` (`src/utils/panelLayoutProjection.ts:126-144`) — so the row is deleted, `activePanelId` becomes undefined, and **zero panel rows remain**. The only "can't close the last pane" protection is the cosmetic `canClosePanel` gate on the X button; the keyboard binding and API callers bypass it.

Consequences of the zero-row state:
- The layout renders an empty canvas (header only).
- NORMAL_MODE is activated per rendered block surface — with no blocks rendered it never activates, so every block-scoped shortcut is dead (j/k, leaders, even Ctrl+W itself). Only GLOBAL actions still work (command palette, and any GLOBAL binding that routes through `navigate()`, which is the accidental escape hatch).
- There is **no runtime repair**: `applyCurrentLayoutUrl` returns `{kind:'empty'}` and does nothing (`src/utils/panelLayoutProjection.ts:709-730`); the empty→landing repair runs only in `bootstrapWorkspace`. A comment in `src/bootstrap/workspaceBootstrap.ts` ("later empty-layout navigation until a full reload") suggests this is at least partially known. In practice the user is stuck until a full reload.

The same state is reachable from the API: `reconcilePanelRows(repo, session, [])`.

**Suggested fix:** guard the last-row case in `deletePanelRow` (either refuse, or swap the pane's content to the `workspaceLandingFacet`-resolved landing block instead of deleting the row) — and/or make the runtime `{kind:'empty'}` result trigger the same landing resolution that bootstrap uses.

## 2. A pane whose block is missing ("Loading block...") strands keyboard nav when it's the active panel

A panel row whose `topLevelBlockId` points at a deleted or never-synced block renders a perpetual `MissingDataRenderer` "Loading block..." (`src/components/renderer/MissingDataRenderer.tsx`) with nothing focusable inside. When that pane is the **active** panel:
- no block inside it can ever be `blockInFocus`,
- every *other* pane fails `panelSurfaceActive` (`activePanelId !== panelId`, `src/extensions/useShortcutSurfaceActivations.ts:65-67`),

so NORMAL_MODE has zero active instances **app-wide** — both panes look fine, but only GLOBAL shortcuts respond. Recovery requires a pointer click on a healthy pane (invisible affordance for a keyboard-driven user); clicking the void pane keeps it active and dead.

Reachable via: any client deleting a block that another pane/device currently displays; stale URLs/sessions carrying since-deleted ids (`parseSlot` treats any token as a block id); API callers passing a bad id.

(Related, now largely mitigated: `reconcilePanelRows` repairs a dangling `activePanelId` via `activePanelIdAfterReconcile` — nice — but the "valid row, missing block" case above has the same user-facing symptom and no repair.)

**Suggested fix:** treat "active panel's block confirmed missing" as repairable — e.g. `MissingDataRenderer` (or the panel shell) offering a close/go-home affordance, or a repair effect that closes/swaps panes whose block is tombstoned.

## 3. `reconcilePanelRows` accepts unvalidated slot ids → ghost rows the URL projection cannot remove

`reconcilePanelRows`/`createPanelRowInTx` accept any string as a target block id, including `''`. An empty-id row renders nothing, and `layoutSlotsFromRows` **drops blockId-less rows from the serialized layout** (`src/utils/panelLayoutProjection.ts:227-228`) — so the ghost row exists in the session and the DOM grid but is invisible to every URL-driven reconcile (`sameLayoutSlots` never sees it), and can never be cleaned up by navigation. Session rows / URL / rendered panes end up mutually inconsistent.

**Suggested fix:** validate/filter slot ids at the `reconcilePanelRows` boundary (non-empty at minimum; optionally `repo.exists` for stronger hygiene given #2).

## Repro (live tab, dev console or agent eval)

```js
const { getUIStateBlock, getLayoutSessionBlock } = await import('@/data/stateBlocks.js')
const { getLayoutSessionId } = await import('@/utils/layoutSessionId.js')
const { reconcilePanelRows } = await import('@/utils/panelLayoutProjection.js')
const ui = await getUIStateBlock(repo, repo.activeWorkspaceId, repo.user, {})
const session = await getLayoutSessionBlock(ui, getLayoutSessionId())
await session.load()

// #1 — empty workspace (or: reduce to one pane and press Ctrl+W)
await reconcilePanelRows(repo, session, [])
// → blank canvas; j/k and leader keys dead; palette works; only reload recovers.

// #2 — void pane; make it active by clicking its (empty) column
await reconcilePanelRows(repo, session, ['00000000-dead-4bad-a000-000000000000', '<some real block id>'])
// → left pane stuck on "Loading block..."; with it active, keyboard dead app-wide.

// #3 — ghost row
await reconcilePanelRows(repo, session, ['', '<some real block id>'])
// → session has 2 panel rows, URL serializes 1, and no navigation removes the ghost.
```

Downstream we're shipping an extension-side watchdog (zero-row repair via `navigate()`, ghost-row cleanup, grace-perioded void-pane swap) as a workaround, but #1 especially feels like it wants the core guard — happy to provide more detail or test a fix.

title: properties-as-children retains a synced parent cache column, so concurrent distinct-key edits still clobber under column-LWW
description:
## Context

Block properties are stored as a single `properties_json` column on the `blocks` row. A single-property mutation rewrites the **whole** column (`txEngine.setProperty` ~L447, `update` ~L358), and sync merges that column with column-level last-write-wins. Two clients concurrently editing *different* keys of the same block (A sets `foo`, B sets `bar`) both PATCH the one column, so the later write silently drops the other's key. This is the known LWW gap documented in `docs/field-level-sync-merge.md` (exploration **on hold**).

The proposed structural alternative — **properties as children** (each property becomes an independently-syncing child block, Tana-style; `docs/properties-model-evolution.md`, plus a spike branch) — was in part motivated by *retiring* the per-key merge plumbing rather than building it (`field-level-sync-merge.md` intro: it "would retire most of the merge plumbing in this doc").

## Problem

The current design/prototype **does not eliminate the clobbering**. Even with each property as its own child row, the parent block still carries a cached `properties_json` projection that must be patched on **every** property mutation — the consistency rule in `properties-model-evolution.md` requires: *"any mutation to a row where `field_id IS NOT NULL` (before or after) must also patch the relevant parent's `properties_json` in the same transaction."*

That consistency story only guarantees **local** cache↔children agreement within one client (its case 8, "remote sync apply", is "handled by atomic local write at origin"). It says nothing about **cross-client merge of the parent cache column**. So two clients editing two *distinct* property-children of the same parent still both write the parent's single `properties_json` column, and it still merges by column-LWW — the exact failure mode the structural move was meant to avoid. Moving the source of truth into child rows doesn't help if the denormalized parent cache is the thing that syncs and merges as one column.

Whether this is silent data loss or merely cache staleness depends on an unresolved question: if the independently-synced child rows are authoritative, the property data itself survives and only the parent's cached projection is clobbered (rebuildable). If the cache is treated as authoritative for the fast-read / cross-block-query path, a block shows stale/missing property values until something rebuilds it.

## Open design questions

- Should the parent `properties_json` cache **sync at all**, or be a pure local projection reconstructed from the (independently-synced) child rows after sync-apply — so the shared column never participates in conflict resolution? This is the cleanest way to actually deliver the clobbering-elimination the structural model promised.
- If the cache **must** sync (to keep cross-block queries fast without hydrating children), does that column need field-level merge anyway — reintroducing the very merge plumbing properties-as-children was meant to retire?
- Interaction with the on-hold `apply_block_patches` per-key merge (`field-level-sync-merge.md` layers A/B/C): is a minimal per-key merge on `properties_json` still needed as a bridge, or does a non-synced/derived cache make it unnecessary?
- Rebuild trigger + cost: if the cache is derived, when is it recomputed (sync-apply tail, lazy on read, dirty-flag), and what is the read-path cost for cross-block property queries that currently hit `properties_json` directly?

## Scope / files
- `src/data/internals/txEngine.ts` (`setProperty`, `update`) — whole-column property writes
- `src/data/blockSchema.ts` — `properties_json` column
- `src/data/blockCache.ts` — row-level LWW acceptance gate (`applyIfNewer`)
- `src/services/powersync.ts` — uploader / column PATCH
- `docs/properties-model-evolution.md` + `docs/field-level-sync-merge.md` — the two design threads to reconcile
- the properties-as-children spike (parent cache retained alongside field-child rows)

## Not in scope
Implementation. This needs a design decision on whether/how the parent property cache participates in sync **before** the properties-as-children model can claim to solve concurrent distinct-key data loss. Filing as a design/architecture record so the "properties-as-children retires the merge problem" assumption isn't inherited unchecked.

title: Consider bundling React same-origin instead of externalizing to esm.sh
description:
## Context

Follow-up from PR #309. React (+ react-dom, scheduler) is currently **externalized to esm.sh** in production via an import map (`vite-plugins/reactImportMapMode.ts`), with SRI integrity. Because those URLs are absolute + cross-origin, they're excluded from the service worker's `dist/`-walking same-origin precache.

In #309 we closed the resulting offline gap with **option A**: the SW now precaches the exact import-map integrity set (the esm.sh React URLs) into its shared vendor cache at install, so a controlled offline load can resolve React. That makes offline work, but keeps the cross-origin dependency and a bespoke vendor-precache path.

This issue tracks **option C**: stop externalizing React and **bundle it same-origin** instead.

## Why it might be worth doing

- **Simpler offline story.** Same-origin React would be emitted under `dist/` and covered automatically by the existing full-graph precache — no separate `precacheVendor` list, no import-map integrity plumbing, no cross-origin `km-vendor` cache.
- **One fewer external dependency at boot.** Today a cold first load reaches esm.sh for React; a same-origin bundle removes that third-party runtime dependency (availability, SRI-pinning, CDN policy).
- **Generation consistency for React too.** Same-origin React would live in each generation's namespaced asset cache like everything else, rather than a shared un-namespaced vendor cache.

## Why we externalized in the first place (trade-offs to weigh)

- esm.sh gives a **shared, immutable, cross-origin-cached** React that multiple deploys/previews reuse without re-downloading.
- Externalizing keeps React **out of the same-origin bundle**, shrinking first-party JS.
- The import map lets **user extensions** import `react`/`react-dom` by bare specifier at runtime and resolve to the same singleton React the app uses. Bundling must preserve this — extensions still need a single shared React instance (e.g. expose it on a same-origin module the import map points at, rather than an esm.sh URL). **This is the load-bearing constraint** and the main reason to think carefully before switching.

## Scope

- Evaluate whether bundling React same-origin (while preserving the single-shared-instance guarantee for user extensions) is worth the bundle-size / CDN-cache trade.
- If yes: point the production import map at a same-origin React module, drop `productionReactIntegrity` + the SW `precacheVendor` path (option A becomes unnecessary), and confirm extensions still resolve one shared React.

Not urgent — offline works today via option A. This is a simplification/robustness question, not a bug.

title: Undo grouping: collapse multi-tx composite operations into one undo entry (merge-at-record)
description:
# Undo grouping: collapse multi-tx composite operations into one undo entry

This issue is a **self-contained handoff**: it assumes you have a checkout of this repo but no other context (no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md conventions loaded, no custom skills). Everything you need — design decisions, file map, invariants, process requirements, and the review protocol — is in here. The design was worked out in a prior session and the decisions below are **settled**; don't re-litigate them, but do flag (in the PR description) anything you discover that genuinely contradicts them.

## Problem

Complex operations that span several `repo.tx` calls produce several entries on the undo stack, so reverting one user-perceived action takes several cmd-Z presses. Canonical case: an SRS reschedule (`rescheduleBlock`, `src/plugins/srs-rescheduling/index.ts:320`) calls `getOrCreateDailyNote` twice (`src/plugins/daily-notes/dailyNotes.ts:172`), each of which may call `getOrCreateJournalBlock` (`dailyNotes.ts:99`) — each helper opens its own tx. On a fresh workspace day one "Good" tap is 2–4 undo entries, and one undo only reverts the property write, stranding the created daily notes. Same shape for any action calling N tx-opening helpers. See `docs/follow-ups.md` ("Reschedule (and similar actions) emit multiple `BlockDefault` txs") and `docs/data-layer-redesign.md` §16.4 (deferred "checkpoints" sketch) for history.

## Settled design

**Merge-at-record undo grouping.** Keep "one committed `repo.tx` = one recording event", but let a composite operation stamp its txs with a shared **group token**. When `UndoManager.record` receives an entry whose `groupId` matches the current top-of-stack entry's `groupId`, it **merges** the new entry's snapshots into the top entry instead of pushing. The stack invariant becomes one entry per user-perceived operation, and everything downstream (`undo()`, `redo()`, `_replay`, `depths()`, toast subscriptions) stays untouched because they only ever see single entries.

The snapshot fold rule already exists: `recordWrite` in `src/data/internals/txSnapshots.ts` — per block id, keep the **earliest** `before`, take the **latest** `after`. Merging a group entry is folding the incoming snapshots map into the existing one with exactly that rule. A merged entry replays identically to what one big tx would have produced (including the inverse-of-create delete branch in `applyRaw`).

Decisions locked in the design session:

1. **Merge-at-record**, not pop-until-boundary at undo time (§16.4's literal sketch) and not a two-level group stack. Rationale: `depths()` stays truthful, toast `peekUndo` checks keep working, undo/redo/replay unchanged.
2. **Per-step metadata retained**: the merged entry keeps a `steps: {txId, description?}[]` array (metadata only, no per-step snapshots) so history/debugging can see what a group contains. Full per-step snapshots (for a future "step into group" undo) are explicitly out of scope.
3. **Token delivery via an explicit facade**, not ambient state: `repo.undoGroup(description, fn)` hands `fn` a `Repo`-shaped facade whose `tx` injects the token. Ambient "current group" state was rejected because a concurrent unrelated write (e.g. a debounced editor save) would get stamped into the group and cmd-Z would then revert the user's text edit together with the operation. With the facade, a wrong merge is structurally impossible — only txs issued through the facade carry the token.
4. **Persist `groupId`** into `tx_context` / `row_events` (local-only audit; no Postgres migration, no PowerSync sync-config change) so the future events-derived undo (§16.6 of the redesign doc) gets group identity for free.
5. **Rollout**: wrap the SRS reschedule action (the known offender) as the proving case, update its toast to group-aware matching. Auto-grouping at the action-dispatch boundary is a **follow-up, not this issue** (see Out of scope).
6. Tx-threading (giving helpers an in-tx variant so an action runs one big tx) remains the preferred pattern *for new code where atomicity matters*, but is **not required here** — grouping is the retrofit net. Don't refactor `getOrCreateDailyNote`/`getOrCreateJournalBlock` signatures.

## Orientation — where things live

Line numbers are anchors as of master at issue-creation time; they may drift a little.

- `src/data/internals/undoManager.ts` — `UndoManager`, `UndoEntry {scope, txId, snapshots, description?}`. Per-workspace × per-scope undo/redo stacks. `record()` clears the redo stack **before** its notify (there's a comment explaining why — preserve that ordering).
- `src/data/repo.ts` — `tx()` records the undo entry post-commit (~line 1004) into `undoManagerFor(result.workspaceId)`; `undo()`/`redo()` (~1049) pop one entry and `_replay` it (~1192) as a single tx driving each id to `before`/`after` via `applyRaw`; failed replays push the entry back. `repo.mutate` is a Proxy built in the constructor with `dispatchMutator.bind(this)` (~line 660) — **bound to the original repo**; see facade gotcha below.
- `src/data/api/tx.ts` — `RepoTxOptions {scope, description?}` (~line 255).
- `src/data/internals/txSnapshots.ts` — `SnapshotsMap = Map<id, {before, after}>`, `recordWrite` fold rule.
- `src/data/internals/txEngine.ts` — sets/clears the single-row `tx_context` table around each writeTransaction; `runTx` returns `{value, txId, workspaceId, snapshots, ...}`.
- `src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts` — `tx_context` table (id/tx_id/tx_seq/user_id/scope/source, ~line 38); `row_events` table (~line 69) + its three insert triggers (~line 420+) which read `tx_context` via `(SELECT … FROM tx_context WHERE id = 1)` and `COALESCE(..., 'sync')`. There is an existing guarded local-schema migration pattern — `PRAGMA table_info` + `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` (~line 1318, used for `user_updated_at`) — follow it.
- `src/plugins/srs-rescheduling/index.ts` — `rescheduleBlock` (~line 320) and the toast-showing call site (~line 401).
- `src/plugins/srs-rescheduling/RescheduleToast.tsx` — Undo button, currently matches "would undo revert exactly my action" by `peekUndo()?.txId === txId` (line ~31).
- Existing tests to extend: `src/data/internals/undoManager.test.ts`, `src/data/test/repoUndo.test.ts`.

## Specification

### 1. `UndoEntry` + `UndoManager.record` merge

- Add `groupId?: string` and `steps: {txId: string, description?: string}[]` to `UndoEntry` (a plain single-tx entry has one step; or keep `steps` optional — your call, but the merged shape must expose per-step txIds/descriptions).
- In `record()`: if the incoming entry has a non-null `groupId` AND the top of that scope's undo stack has the **same** `groupId`, fold the incoming snapshots into the top entry (per id: keep existing `before`, take incoming `after`; insert ids not yet present — reuse/mirror `recordWrite`), append the step, and keep the entry's `description` as the group description. Otherwise push as today.
- A merged record still **clears the redo stack** and still notifies subscribers (it is "a new action landed"). Preserve the existing clear-before-notify ordering.
- Merging must only ever apply to the **contiguous top of stack**. If a foreign (ungrouped or different-group) entry landed in between, the group simply splits into two entries — degraded but correct. Never search below the top.
- Zero-write txs (`snapshots.size === 0`) stay no-ops.

### 2. `repo.undoGroup` + facade

- `RepoTxOptions` gains `undoGroup?: {id: string, description: string}` (exact shape yours; the id must reach the recorded `UndoEntry.groupId` and the engine so it can be written to `tx_context`).
