That's the existing override mechanism — plugins replace kernel registrations by registering after them. It works, but the warn is easy to miss and accidental name collisions silently overwrite intended behavior.

## Current state (verified)

All ~8 facets in `src/data/facets.ts` use an identical combine: build a `Map<string, …>`, `console.warn` on duplicate, `set` (last-wins). No `overrides` field, no throw-on-collision.

## Fix shape

Registrations may opt into a checked override target:

```ts
propertySchemasFacet.of(statusPropV2, {source: 'my-plugin', overrides: 'status'})
```

`combine` asserts an entry under `overrides` exists; if absent, **throw** (catches typos). If present, replace silently (intent declared, no warn). Without `overrides`, any duplicate-name collision **throws** (catches accidents). Strict mode + intentional override + typo catch in one shape. ~10 lines per facet's combine; apply uniformly.

**Trigger to build:** plugin authors stepping on each other's schema/mutator/processor names in the wild and warn-and-last-wins not catching it in review. Until then the existing convention works for the alpha-stage plugin surface.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2)._

title: Drop unflushed ps_crud for local-only mode (and reduce import bloat)
description:
## Problem

`ps_crud` is PowerSync's outgoing upload queue. The Roam import (run with `source='user'`) enqueued 304k rows ≈ 204 MB. In `localOnly` mode (no remote sync) those entries can never drain; with remote sync on but a massive import, the queue still bloats local storage until it drains.

## Current state (verified)

- `TxSource` is only `'user'` (`src/data/api/changeScope.ts`); all `ChangeScope` entries map to `source='user'`.
- Roam import uses default `repo.tx(...)` (source `'user'`) — `src/plugins/roam-import/import.ts`.
- No `discardPendingUploads` action exists.

## Two angles

- **Cleanup option** — when `localOnly` is active, expose a `discardPendingUploads()` action that truncates `ps_crud` (or raw `DELETE FROM ps_crud`, since nothing reads it locally). Frees ~200 MB on this DB.
- **Don't enqueue during import** — the upload trigger gates on `tx_context.source = 'user'`. Add a fourth source value `'import'`; both the upload trigger and `row_events` trigger learn to ignore it; the Roam import wraps its txs with `source: 'import'`. Then both `ps_crud` AND `row_events` stay small even on bulk import (the latter trims an additional ~250 MB of audit bloat — overlaps with the row_events-trim issue).

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2)._

title: Periodic row_events trim (bound the per-row audit log)
description:
## Problem

`row_events` is the per-row audit + invalidation log. It is trigger-written and **never trimmed** — it grew to 262 MB / 304k rows on the import-heavy DB. The fast path doesn't need history; the row_events tail consumes by ascending `id` and only needs rows newer than its high-watermark. Long-tail entries are dead weight on disk and on backup/export.

## Current state (verified)

- `row_events` defined in `src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts` with AUTOINCREMENT id, no trim logic.
- No `DELETE FROM row_events` anywhere; only `MAX(id)` reads for watermark tracking (`rowEventsTail.ts`).

## Fix shape

At startup (or on a low-priority idle hook), `DELETE FROM row_events WHERE id < (MAX(id) - K)` for some K (e.g. 50 000), or `WHERE created_at < ?` with a 7-day window. Either runs in one statement; the index on `id` is the auto PK. Optional: bound `command_events` with the same shape (small today, same unbounded shape).

Note: PowerSync's CRUD-apply path writes a row_event per sync write, so even a fully-synced read-only client accumulates. Worth doing.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2)._

title: Reduce per-block flicker on lazy hierarchical loads — wrap expand toggles in useTransition
description:
## Problem

`useChildIds` is backed by `repo.childIds`, which hydrates the whole children list per parent on first read. That keeps the per-parent expand path fast, but as the user scrolls into deeper levels their grandchildren still load on `LazyBlockComponent` mount and visibly pop in.

## Current state (verified) — most of this is already done

- ✅ **Structural skeleton**: `src/components/BlockLoadingPlaceholder.tsx` already renders a `BulletDot` at the right indent inside a block-shaped flex layout (not a bare 32px `<div>`).
- ✅ **Overscan**: `OVERSCAN_PX = 600` in `src/components/LazyBlockComponent.tsx`.
- ✅ **`repo.childIds`** id-only query (`core.childIds`) backs `useChildIds`.
- ❌ **`useTransition` around expand toggles** — NOT done. `DefaultBlockRenderer` calls `await setIsCollapsed(!isCollapsed)` directly with no `startTransition`.

## Remaining work

`startTransition`-wrap the `setIsCollapsed` write so React keeps showing the previous tree until the new descendant Suspense boundaries resolve, instead of flashing fallbacks during the load window. (`src/components/renderer/DefaultBlockRenderer.tsx`.)

Optional, if it still feels jumpy after that: tighter overscan / prefetch — warm a few levels of `repo.childIds` ahead of intersection.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2). Scope reduced: skeleton + overscan already shipped; only the `useTransition` piece remains._

title: Move properties_json / references_json to JSONB across the data layer
description:
## Problem

`properties_json` and `references_json` are stored as `text` everywhere — Postgres column, PowerSync sync stream, local SQLite. There are ~29 `json_extract` / `json_each` callsites over these columns (including per-write triggers in `src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts` on `$.alias` and `$.types`) that re-parse the whole text blob on every call. JSONB would walk the binary structure directly — bigger blobs and hotter paths get the bigger win.

## Current state (verified)

- `src/data/blockSchema.ts`: `properties_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`, `references_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` (Postgres + local SQLite).
- `blockToRowParams` still does `JSON.stringify(...)` for both.
- Read path wraps in `json(properties_json)` / `json(references_json)`.

Out of scope for the per-key `properties_json` merge work (`docs/field-level-sync-merge.md`): the correctness fix doesn't need it, and the migration has a real rollout-compat problem worth handling in isolation (old clients send `JSON.stringify(properties)` strings; a string body in a `jsonb` column stores a JSONB *string scalar*, not the object).

## Fix shape (when triggered)

- Bundle the Postgres column migration with the client uploader change that sends objects/arrays instead of strings.
- Defensive server-side normalization for inflight stringified writes during rollout: `CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(properties_json) = 'string' THEN properties_json #>> '{}' ELSE properties_json END`.
- Re-create `idx_blocks_workspace_with_references` with the jsonb predicate (`references_json <> '[]'::jsonb`).
- Local side: confirm wa-sqlite supports SQLite 3.45+ JSONB; wrap each `SELECT properties_json` in `json(properties_json)` so the JS driver still gets text; change pull-down `put` SQL to `jsonb(?)`; verify the shape of `CrudEntry.previousValues.properties_json`.
- **Benchmark** on a representative block count (import-heavy DB) before committing — the win has to be measured.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2)._

title: Schema-rename does not cascade — instance values orphan on rename
description:
## Problem

When a user renames a `property-schema` block (editing `property-schema:name` via `PropertySchemaBlockRenderer`), the schema republishes under the new name but every instance block's `properties_json` is still keyed by the **OLD** name. The old name has values but no schema; the new name has a schema but no values. **The renamed property silently disappears from the UI** (and its data is effectively orphaned).

## Current state (verified)

- `PropertySchemaBlockRenderer.writeName` only calls `block.set(propertyNameProp, next)` — it updates the schema block's name and nothing else.
- `properties_json` is keyed by `schema.name` (`src/data/block.ts` reads `data.properties[schema.name]`).
- No cascade-rename, no block-id keying.

## Two viable fixes

- **Cascade-rename**: on schema name change, walk every block where `properties_json` has the old key and rewrite the key to the new name in one tx. Surgical; no data-model change. Cost: high-fanout schemas (e.g. renaming `status` across 50K blocks) rewrite a lot of rows under PowerSync's serialized writer; mid-rename conflict resolution must handle blocks transiently carrying both keys.
- **Block-id keying** (see companion issue): `properties_json` keys become schema block-ids. Renames become free at the value layer. Requires resolving "what's the block-id for a kernel/plugin schema?" and a one-time migration of every existing `properties_json` blob.

User is leaning toward **block-id keying as the destination** (composes with the "id-stable handle" decision for types). Cascade-rename remains a viable interim step that doesn't paint into a corner.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P2). Companion to the block-id-keying issue._

title: CI guard on Postgres ↔ TS schema drift
description:
## Problem

`scripts/gen-sync-config.ts` keeps the local-SQLite raw-table mapping and the PowerSync sync-stream SELECT in lockstep (both projected from `BLOCK_STORAGE_COLUMNS` / `WORKSPACE_*` arrays), and `check:sync-config` enforces TS ↔ PowerSync consistency in CI. **But Postgres is still drift-prone** — someone can edit `BLOCK_STORAGE_COLUMNS` without writing the matching `supabase/migrations/<…>.sql`, and nothing fails until `db push` (or worse, a runtime PATCH referencing a missing column).

## Current state (verified)

- `check:sync-config` runs via `yarn run check` (`scripts/check.mjs`, `.github/workflows/run-tests.yml`) — validates TS ↔ PowerSync only.
- `BLOCK_STORAGE_COLUMNS` lives in `src/data/blockSchema.ts`.
- **No** Postgres-drift CI step, **no** `yarn snapshot:schema` script, **no** `supabase/schema-snapshot.json`.

## Fix shape

A CI step that asserts the Postgres column set is a **superset** of every name in the TS column lists. Options:

- Query the linked DB: `npx supabase db query --linked "SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name IN ('blocks','workspaces','workspace_members')"` and diff against the TS arrays. Cost: needs a Supabase-reachable env in CI.
- Or a checked-in `supabase/schema-snapshot.json` regenerated via `yarn snapshot:schema` and diffed (no live DB).
- Lower-effort variant: parse migration files as text and grep for `add column.*<name>` per TS column — no DB connection, but misses dropped columns.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P1). Note: partial mitigation (`check:sync-config`) already exists; this covers the Postgres gap specifically._

title: Action/context resolution: filters can only opt in (OR), so modal contexts can't yield to text editing
description:
## Problem

The reconciler decides whether to handle a key event by **OR-ing** the `eventFilter` of every active context:

```ts
// src/shortcuts/HotkeyReconciler.tsx:90
for (const type of active.keys()) {
  if (config?.eventFilter?.(event)) return true   // any filter can opt IN
}
return defaultEventFilter(event)
```

Because composition is OR-only, an `eventFilter` can **only widen** the set of handled events — it can never veto. Concretely, `EDIT_MODE_CM`'s filter returns `true` for events inside `.cm-editor` (`src/shortcuts/defaultContexts.ts:48`), opting editor events *back into* dispatch. When a modal context is active at the same time (e.g. SRS review's reveal/grade context over a revealed-answer CodeMirror), it shadows edit-mode and eats keys like Enter / 1‑4 while the user is typing. There's no way for the modal context to declaratively say "I yield while focus is in an editor."

The current workaround (PR #63, `src/plugins/srs-review/ReviewSession.tsx`) gates at *activation*: deactivate the whole context when focus lands on an editable element (`isEditableElement`). This works but:
- pushes focus→activation plumbing into each feature component;
- re-implements editable-target detection that already exists (`isEditorElement` / `shouldExitEditModeAfterBlur`, `src/utils/dom.ts:37`);
- will be copy-pasted by every future modal context.

## Direction (general, not a single point-fix)

Rather than only adding a `suppressInEditableTarget` flag, rework how the reconciler **resolves which active context wins an event** so that suppression/veto is expressible centrally. Things to weigh:

1. **Tri-state filters** — `handle` / `ignore` / `veto`, so a context can actively suppress lower-priority contexts instead of only opting in.
2. **Precedence-based single-winner resolution** — modal/exclusive contexts declare higher precedence; the reconciler picks one winning context per event rather than OR-ing all filters.
3. **Declarative editable-target awareness** — e.g. `suppressInEditableTarget` / `modal` flags evaluated centrally against the shared `isEditorElement` helper, so features stop hand-rolling focus gating. (This is the cheap subset of the above and could ship first to retire the PR #63 workaround.)

## Acceptance
- A modal context can declaratively yield to text editing (no per-component focus gating).
- Editable-target detection lives in one place (reuse `src/utils/dom.ts`).
- Document the new resolution/precedence semantics; existing single-context behavior preserved.
- As a follow-up, delete the `surfaceFocused` / `isEditableElement` workaround in `ReviewSession.tsx`.

Context: surfaced during PR #63 (spaced-repetition review UI).

title: appMountsFacet (and id-bearing facets) should dedup by logical `id`, not just FacetContribution reference
description:
## Problem

The resolver dedups contributions by **`FacetContribution` object identity**:

```ts
// src/extensions/resolveAppRuntime.ts:158
if (seen.has(node)) return
seen.add(node)
```

This is the right granularity for **reference-stable, idempotent** contributions — e.g. exported singleton data/schema extensions like `dailyNotesDataExtension`. Every plugin that bundles the same exported object hits `seen.has(node)` and it registers exactly once.

It is the **wrong** granularity for app mounts. `appMountsFacet` uses the default combine, which keeps every value:

```ts
// src/extensions/facet.ts:83
combine: combine ?? (values => values as unknown as Output)   // keeps all
```

and mounts are contributed *inside plugin factories*, so each call mints a fresh `FacetContribution`:

```ts
// src/plugins/daily-notes/index.ts:196
appMountsFacet.of(reschedulePickerMount, {source: 'daily-notes'}),
```

`AppMountContribution` carries an `id` (e.g. `'daily-notes.reschedule-picker'`) that *looks* like an identity key, but the combine ignores it — it's only metadata. So if two code paths each contribute the same logical mount (e.g. daily-notes and some plugin that wants to "bundle" the picker), reference dedup never fires and **both render**. For the reschedule picker that means two `<ReschedulePicker/>`, two `window.addEventListener(openReschedulePickerEvent, …)` (`src/plugins/daily-notes/ReschedulePicker.tsx:168`), and a single dispatch handled twice.

This is the trap that made bundling the picker mount unsafe in the SRS-review work (PR #63) — we had to gate / treat daily-notes as a hard dep instead of re-contributing the mount.

## Proposal

Give `appMountsFacet` (and any other facet whose values carry a logical `id`) an **id-keyed combine** that collapses duplicates by `id` — last-wins or first-wins, whichever we standardize — so a logically-singleton mount stays single no matter how many plugins reference it.

Options to consider:
- An id-dedup combine specifically on `appMountsFacet`.
- A small reusable `dedupById` combine helper for any id-bearing facet.
- A dev-mode warning when two surviving contributions share an `id` (catches accidental double-mounts even where last-wins is "fine").

## Acceptance
- Two contributions of the same mount `id` result in a single mount.
- Existing single-contribution behavior unchanged.
- Decide + document the tie-break (precedence/order) for same-`id` collisions.

Context: surfaced during PR #63 (spaced-repetition review UI).

title: searchSourcesFacet: decide payload authority by source declaration, not timestamp archaeology
description:
Deferred design call surfaced while fixing the duplicate-payload merge (GH #450 / PR #449). Not urgent: core.content is the only registered search source today, so duplicate groups are always size 1 and none of this is reachable in production yet.

When two sources return the SAME block, the merge point must pick which copy of the block the user sees. Today it infers that from block.userUpdatedAt carried inside each copy — newest copy wins. That is an indirect proxy: it deduces the age of the snapshot from a field written inside the snapshot.

Alternative: let a source declare its authority. core.content reads live from SQLite on every call, so it is authoritative by construction; {id: 'core.content', authoritative: true} would let its payload win outright, with timestamps only breaking ties between non-authoritative sources.

Why it may be worth doing: the timestamp proxy has failure modes the declaration does not — a source that hand-builds BlockData and omits or mis-copies userUpdatedAt, or a remote index with clock skew. And it is far easier to explain to a plugin author ('core's copy wins; yours is used when core did not return that block') than a timestamp tournament.

Cheap to add while there is one source; awkward once a plugin depends on the timestamp rule.

title: Alias/content search is ASCII-only case-insensitive (SQLite LOWER/LIKE)
description:
SQLite's built-in LOWER() and case-insensitive LIKE are ASCII-only. Verified empirically: LOWER('É') stays 'É', and 'Émile' LIKE '%émi%' does not match.

Scope: this is uniform across every alias/content search call site, not specific to one query builder. aliasesInWorkspace SQL-LOWERs both sides consistently and is affected the same way as the JS/SQL-mixed buildFuzzyAliasMatchesSql path. It is a pre-existing limitation of the storage engine, not something escapeLikePattern causes or could fix.

User-visible effect: searching a non-ASCII term finds nothing unless the case matches exactly — 'émile' does not find a block containing 'Émile'.

Options if we want full-Unicode case-insensitive search:
- SQLite's ICU extension (adds a build/runtime dependency)
- app-side case folding into a normalized column written at write time, plus a migration and a backfill for existing rows

Found while writing the search-merge fuzz suites (GH #432 / PR #449). That suite's unicode generator is deliberately scoped to case-invariant code points (CJK, emoji, NBSP-class whitespace) so this limitation does not contaminate an unrelated property; noted in the suite docblock.

title: Unify derivation passes behind version-stamped gating
description:
TRIGGER-GATED — do not do this now. Build when one of the derivation passes next needs a forced re-run, or when a fifth is added.

Four one-shot derivation passes each hand-roll their own gating on top of the shared PendingIdleJobs + MarkerStore (src/data/internals/idleMarkerJobs.ts):
- scheduleWorkspaceRefBackfill (marker reproject_ref:)
- scheduleReferenceTargetDerivePass (SESSION-only Set, unlike its siblings)
- scheduleReconcileRescan (marker reconcile_rescan_v1:)
- LocalSchema backfills (block_aliases / block_types / fts, once per DB)

All rebuild LOCAL state that is a pure function of local rows: never upload, safe read-only, idempotent, correctly per-device.

Proposal: replace the one-shot marker with a VERSION STAMP — store the deriver's version, re-run when the code's version exceeds it. Two payoffs: retires the hand-bumped id hack (daily-note-date-from-alias-v2 had to change its id to force a re-run) and fixes the session-vs-persistent gating inconsistency nobody chose.

Explicitly NOT in scope: WorkspaceBackfill / workspaceBackfillsFacet. That is the other family — it repairs source-of-truth rows and uploads, so it is once-per-GRAPH with different requirements. Merging the two is what produced the shape mismatch documented in AGENTS.md. See PR #508.

title: Revisit bd upgrade when a tested 1.2.x ships
description:
Pinned to bd 1.2.2, which is the tested 1.1.2 code re-released under a higher version. The real 1.2.x features (work leases, events journal, sync federation, HTTP API server, provenance events) plus the prime memory-cap config are not in it and return in a later tested release.

When that lands: upgrade every machine/clone before touching the DB, then re-evaluate whether the prime hook still needs the --mcp workaround for memory injection, and whether the schema cursor rolls forward cleanly from v53.

Blocked on upstream. See memory project_beads_121_schema_recovery for the traps.

title: REALIGN_WINDOW_MS has no behavioural test, and can't get a freeze-tolerant one
description:
`REALIGN_WINDOW_MS` (250ms, src/utils/panelScrollAnchor.ts) has no test under it: mutating it to 0 leaves src/utils/test/panelScrollAnchor.test.ts fully green (verified on PR #572). Same was true of ROW_WAIT_MS until #572 added `still honours an anchor that hydrates hundreds of ms late`, which works because 2000ms leaves room for a 400ms delay.

That trick does not transfer. Any test of "the correction window is still open at time T" needs T < 250ms of REAL time, and a frozen worker (see km-scji / #571) loses whole seconds — so on resume the correction timer expires ahead of the re-check and the test flakes. A behavioural floor under a 250ms constant is not freeze-tolerant by construction.

Fix needs an injectable clock: let alignScrollportToRow take its timer source (or fake timers for that one test) so the window can be advanced deterministically instead of waited out. Then assert both edges — still correcting just inside the window, stopped just outside — which also covers the expiry side, currently untested as well.

Memories: [[testing_budget_ladder_for_freeze_tolerant_tests]], [[testing_model_a_stalled_worker_with_sigstop]].

title: Stale routing.ts:<line> refs in routing.fuzz.test.ts docblock
description:
The docblock and inline comments of src/utils/test/routing.fuzz.test.ts cite routing.ts line numbers that have all drifted (routing.ts:127, :134, :128, :160,168, :184-185, :198-199, :201-251, :232, :242, :260-277, :279-286, :294-301, :237-251, :59-60/249, :94-109, :203, :218, :146-193). PR #566 corrected only the two adjacent to its change.

Line-number refs rot on every edit to routing.ts and a wrong one is worse than none. Replace them with symbol names (parseContextEntries, buildContextSuffix, REST_ENTRY_RE, splitTopLevel, ...) so they stay correct.

Surfaced while fixing #565.
close_reason: Done in PR #566 — resolved by deleting the stale docblock rather than re-pointing its refs at symbol names.

title: Maximizing a pane inside a scrolled stack does not carry the scroll position over
description:
Raised by Codex on [PR #549](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/549#discussion_r3786763879).

Maximizing a pane that lives in a scrolled stack switches the scroll container: the stack column stops being the scroll box and the pane gains its own scrollport, whose offset is unrelated (usually 0). The user lands somewhere other than where they were looking.

**Not a regression from #549 — the same transition happened before it, only worse.** The scroll container swap is inherent to `stackedPanel: true → false`, which both the old (hoist the leaf to top level) and new (prune to the path) implementations perform. The old one additionally remounted the pane, so the position was definitely lost.

**One way #549 could have made it subtly different, unverified:** removing the remount also removes whatever the remount used to trigger, and the panel has a post-render scroll-restore path (`consumeRestore()`). If that restore is what used to land the pane somewhere sensible, a preserved component no longer runs it. This is a hypothesis from reading `PanelRenderer`; I did not confirm it, and a browser probe was inconclusive because the pane chrome scrolls out of view at the offsets involved.

**Fix direction:** transfer the stack column's `scrollTop` onto the pane's scrollport when entering the solo path and back when leaving, or anchor on the focused row via the existing `alignScrollportToRow` machinery (see #513, which makes the cursor the scroll position — that may already be the intended answer).

title: Maximizing a pane rebuilds the CodeMirror editor inside it
description:
Found during live browser QA of [PR #549](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/549). Affects **all** panes, including top-level ones that PR #549 does not change, so it is not introduced by the maximize work — but maximize is the gesture that triggers it.

**Observed**, with an open editor in a pane, comparing the stashed `.cm-content` node before and after:

| action | pane node | editor node |
|---|---|---|
| toggle sidebar (neutral chrome click, layout width changes) | same | **same** |
| maximize a top-level pane | same | **rebuilt** (old node `isConnected: false`) |
| maximize a stacked pane (after PR #549) | same | **rebuilt** |

So it is specific to maximize rather than generic blur-on-click: a neutral chrome click preserves the editor node, maximize does not. Text content survives (it is in the DB), but the CodeMirror instance is new, which means undo history and selection are lost.

**Hypothesis, not verified:** the trigger is the `wideScrollSurface` flip, which is the thing that differs between the two cases above. `PanelRenderer` already keeps its content frame permanently mounted and only swaps its class for exactly this reason (see the comment on the content frame), so whatever rebuilds the editor is below that frame. Worth confirming before fixing.

title: Unhandled rejection when a view transition is aborted
description:
Noticed while working on [PR #549](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/549); **pre-existing**, not introduced there.

`withMoveTransition` (`src/utils/viewTransition.ts`) awaits only `updateCallbackDone`. When a view transition is aborted — a second transition starting before the first finishes, which panel navigation can do — the `ready`/`finished` promises reject with nothing attached, surfacing as an unhandled rejection in the console.

**Fix direction:** attach a no-op catch to the promises that are not awaited, so an abort is swallowed as the non-event it is, rather than left dangling. Worth a test that starts a second transition while the first is in flight.

title: Panel Forward chevron does not restore the maximize state it left
description:
Deferred from [PR #549](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/549) ([thread](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/549#discussion_r3779746526)).

Closing a nested video-notes visit goes back and un-maximizes in the same tx. The forward entry records the snapshotter's focus, scroll and view mode, but no maximize state, so `goForwardInPanel` has nothing to replay.

Clicking the panel's **Forward** chevron therefore reopens the notes visit **un-maximized**, unlike both the visit the user left and browser Forward through the serialized `;max` URL — two forward affordances that disagree.

Deliberately deferred rather than dismissed: it is a real inconsistency, but a cosmetic one (the pane is re-maximizable by hand) and the design question underneath is genuinely open — see `docs/video-notes-navigation-native.html` §4.4.

**Open design question:** is pane arrangement part of a *visit* (so `VisitState` should carry `maximized` and back/forward should replay it), or is it ambient layout that history should leave alone? Answering that decides the fix; adding a field to `VisitState` before deciding would encode one answer silently.

title: Wikilinks inside code spans/fences still mint references
description:
Raised by Codex on #540 and deliberately **not** fixed there. Filing so the tradeoff is recorded rather than lost in a review thread.

### The gap

`buildSourcePlan` parses `[[…]]` and `((uuid))` out of **raw** `blocks.content`. The markdown pipeline that actually *renders* the block does not — remark treats fenced and inline code as `code`/`inlineCode` nodes, and `remark-wikilinks` only visits `text` nodes.

So for an ordinary (non-extension) block containing:

    Use `const re = /[[\]]/` to escape.

…the reference index records an alias the user never sees rendered as a link. Content and index disagree.

### Why #540 didn't fix it

#540 closes the *catastrophic* instance of this — extension source blocks, which are 100% code — and bounds the blast radius with `MAX_ALIAS_LENGTH`. Making the whole pipeline markdown-aware is a different and much larger change:

- `parseReferencesMarkdownAware` already exists in `referenceParser.ts` and skips `code`/`inlineCode`, but **nothing calls it** — its own docblock notes the plain-text parser is preferred for hot paths.
- Switching would **retroactively drop every existing reference derived from inside a code span**. Against ~31k live aliases with no migration and no way to tell an intentional-but-code-adjacent link from an accidental one, that is a live-data change requiring its own plan — not a review fix.
- The AST parser's index positions are node-relative (see its own comment), so the rewriters (`rewriteWikilinks`, rename, merge-retarget) can't consume its output as-is. It isn't a drop-in.
- Blockrefs would need the same treatment, and `((uuid))` is already anchored to a strict UUID shape, so its accidental-match rate is far lower.

### If picked up

Wants: a decision on existing derived refs (keep-and-grandfather vs drop), absolute position tracking in the markdown-aware parser, coverage for both grammars, and a check on what the CodeMirror decorators (`codeMirrorExtensions.ts`, `wikilinkDecorator.ts`) highlight — they should agree with whichever rule wins.

title: Legacy readwise.js data: four readwise:* properties have mismatched presets, no migration
description:
Found while retiring the superseded `agent-extensions/readwise.js` prototype (#492). The two implementations registered the **same** `readwise:*` property names with **different** presets, so data written by the retired prototype does not match the schemas the surviving `readwise.tsx` declares.

| property | retired `.js` preset | current `.tsx` preset |
|---|---|---|
| `readwise:user_book_id` | `string` | `optional-string` |
| `readwise:highlight_id` | `string` | `optional-string` |
| `readwise:author` | `optional-string` | `ref`, `targetTypes: [PAGE_TYPE]` |
| `readwise:location` | `optional-number` | `optional-string` |

All four verified against both files' source (the `.js` side reads from `git show <the deletion commit>^:agent-extensions/readwise.js`).

### Symptom, and the mechanism — which is *not* a decode failure

For a document whose `readwise:author` was written as a plain author name by the prototype:

`ref`'s `decode` is literally `stringCodec.decode` ([`codecs.ts:181-186`](../blob/master/src/data/api/codecs.ts#L181)) — it checks only `typeof j === 'string'` and performs **no** block-existence or target-type validation. So the legacy plain-string author **decodes cleanly; nothing throws and nothing is swallowed**. The failure is one layer downstream: the author name is then treated as a block id, `repo.block(authorId)` resolves to nothing, `label` is falsy, and `ReadwiseAuthorLine` returns `null`. The author line silently renders nothing.

Flagging the mechanism explicitly because "fix the decode" is the wrong framing — there is no caught decode exception to go hunting for.

The one case that *does* throw is a legacy `null` author (`.js` wrote `book.author ?? null`) meeting `ref`'s decode, which has no null handling, unlike `optional-ref`.

### Scope — likely small, and unconfirmed

- **No data-loss path.** The prototype wrote raw JSON through `tx.create`, which never validates against a schema, so no write gets clobbered either then or now. This is a display/rendering gap only.
- **Not affected by the file deletion.** Installed extension source and materialized data live in the DB, not the repo tree; deleting the repo file changes nothing for anyone already running the prototype. It only makes a *new* `.js` install require resurrecting the source from git history.
- **No migration exists.** Searched `src/` for any backfill touching `readwise:author`/`location`/`user_book_id`/`highlight_id` — nothing.
- **Whether any live client actually holds prototype-shaped data is unverified** (the agent bridge wasn't paired when this was written). If nobody ever ran the `.js` version against real data, this is closeable as moot — worth checking before doing any work here.

### If it turns out to matter

A one-shot backfill over blocks carrying `readwise:*` properties: resolve each plain-string `readwise:author` to (or create) an author page block and rewrite the property as a real ref; coerce `readwise:location` to string; drop legacy `null` authors. Per the repo's convention on imported-source properties, write the typed property *alongside* the origin-tagged `readwise:*` values, never instead of them.

title: Paste-before onto a blank block reverses the pasted order (vim Shift+P, multi-select paste-before)
description:
Found during adversarial review of #491 by two independent reviewers, each reproducing it with concrete values. **Pre-existing and unrelated to that PR** — verified byte-for-byte identical before and after it.

## Repro

Siblings `A, B, C` where `B` is blank. Paste `"Alpha\nBeta\nGamma"` onto `B` with `position: 'before'`:

- expected: `[A, Alpha, Beta, Gamma, C]`
- actual: `[A, Beta, Gamma, Alpha, C]`

## Cause

In `pasteMultilineText` (`src/paste/operations.ts`), a blank target absorbs pasted root #1 — but the absorbed root keeps *the target's own order key*, which doesn't move. Roots #2..N are then placed by `insertionForSiblingRun`'s `before` branch, which computes keys strictly *below* that unmoved key. So root #1 sorts after roots #2..N.

`absorbedRoot = parsedRoots[0]` is chosen independently of `position`, so nothing reconciles "which pasted root the target became" with "which side of the target the run goes on".

## Reachable from

- vim normal mode `Shift+P` — `paste_before`, `src/plugins/vim-normal-mode/actions.ts:282`
- multi-select `paste_before_selection` — `src/shortcuts/defaultShortcuts.ts:1290`

Not reachable from ordinary `Cmd+V` on either surface (both use `position: 'after'`).

## Note on #491's fix

That fix forces `placement: 'sibling'` when absorbing, but it is a **no-op for `position: 'before'`**: the only placement-sensitive clause in `resolveRootDestination` also requires `position === 'after'`, so the branch is unreachable here either way. This needs its own fix.

## Adjacent gaps found in the same review

- `src/paste/test/operations.fuzz.test.ts` only fuzzes the pure planners (`planEditModeMultilinePaste`, `planSingleBlockPaste`, `pasteChordIntent`) — it never exercises the DB-effecting placement logic in `pasteMultilineText` / `pasteEditModeMultilineText`. No fuzz oracle could have caught this class of bug. A property like "pasted roots appear in clipboard order, contiguously, on whichever side `position` names" would cover it.
- `resolveRootDestination`'s `throw new Error('paste target ... has no visible insertion parent')` is dead code: `rootsAsChildren` is already forced true whenever `target.parentId === null`, so `!rootParentId` cannot fire.

title: Resolve the two core→plugin edges the boundary lint rule had to grandfather
description:
The `boundary/no-core-to-plugin-imports` ESLint rule now enforces the central architecture principle — **core cannot depend on plugins; plugins may depend on core and on each other** — across `src/` (composition root exempt, tests exempt).

Three imports in two files had to be grandfathered with inline `eslint-disable` comments:

- `src/extensions/appUpdateStatus.ts` → `@/plugins/diagnostics/facet.js`
- `src/extensions/extensionPromptStatus.ts` → `@/plugins/diagnostics/facet.js`
- `src/extensions/extensionPromptStatus.ts` → `@/plugins/extensions-settings/actions.js`

## Why they're real, not noise

Both modules are core (they project core-owned state — the service-worker app-update signal, and the extension-prompt store — into a status snapshot), and both contribute to `diagnosticsFacet`, which is declared in `src/plugins/diagnostics/facet.ts` under an explicit header:

> Deliberately NOT in core: the only thing core truly owns is the indicator surface itself; the diagnostics concept lives in the plugin layer […]

Core contributing to a facet that documents itself as plugin-layer is a contradiction; one of the two statements has to give.

## The two ways out

1. **Move `diagnosticsFacet` down into core** (`src/facets/` or `src/extensions/core.ts`). Contradicts the facet's stated intent, but core now has two genuine health signals of its own, which is evidence the concept is not plugin-only. The `diagnostics` plugin keeps `useDiagnostics` + the chip UI.
2. **Move the two status projections up into the plugin layer.** `appUpdateStatus.ts` has a plausible home in the existing `update-indicator` plugin; `extensionPromptStatus.ts` is more awkward, since the extension-prompt machinery around it (`extensionPromptStore`, `extensionPromptMount`) is core.

(1) looks cheaper and more honest about where diagnostics actually sits; (2) is more faithful to the original design note. Needs a call before anyone starts.

Not urgent — the edges are static, inline-justified, and the rule prevents *new* ones (the disables are per-import, so another plugin import in either file still fails the gate).

title: Consider canonical-block cloning (or a canonical-source export) for default workspace content
description:
## Pain point

Settings are per-user-**per-workspace**, not per-user. Concretely: enabling "Vim normal mode" (`src/plugins/vim-normal-mode/index.ts`, a `systemToggle`) in one workspace has no effect in any other workspace — it has to be re-enabled every time you open/create a new workspace. Most of what's stored this way isn't actually about the *workspace's content* — it's a preference about how the editor behaves for this person, and should follow them everywhere.

## Current model

Every settings/UI-state block is rooted at a per-`(workspace, user)` "user page", built from deterministic ids over `(workspaceId, userId)` (`userPageBlockId` in `src/data/stateBlocks.ts`). `getUserPrefsBlock` and `getPluginPrefsBlock` walk down from that page, so *every* `ChangeScope.UserPrefs` (and `ChangeScope.UiState`) row a plugin writes is implicitly workspace-scoped — there's no user-level identity in the data model that spans workspaces.

Concretely, for the vim example: the toggle's on/off state lives in a shared `extensions:overrides` map (`src/plugins/extensions-settings/config.ts`), stored on a `getPluginPrefsBlock` row keyed by `(workspace, user, "extensions-prefs")`. Keybinding remaps (`src/plugins/keybindings-settings/overrideStore.ts`) work the same way — one prefs block per workspace. Theme is the odd one out: it lives purely in browser `localStorage` (`src/plugins/theme-toggle/theme.ts`), so it's already effectively "global" per browser profile, but as a tradeoff it does **not** sync across the user's devices the way the workspace-scoped prefs blocks do.

## Rough classification

**Plausibly workspace-scoped** (references this graph's own content): grouped-backlinks' tag priority/exclusion lists (`src/plugins/grouped-backlinks/config.ts`), block-tagging's configured tag list (`src/plugins/block-tagging/config.ts`) — these name tags/pages that only make sense inside one graph.

**Plausibly user-global** (about the editor, not the graph): vim normal mode and its Colemak sub-toggle, most other extension enable/disable toggles, keybinding overrides, theme.

**Ambiguous**: the `extensions:overrides` map bundles *every* togglable's on/off state into one per-workspace row, so splitting out "vim mode" means splitting that map by tier, not just relocating the whole block.

## Storage-location question (open)

The sync model is fundamentally workspace-partitioned: per `powersync/sync-config.yaml`, the only synced tables are `workspaces`, `workspace_members`, and `blocks` (every row of which carries a `workspace_id` and syncs only to members of that workspace). There's no `users`/`profiles`-style table synced independent of workspace membership today — so a tier that's genuinely global (synced across the user's devices, independent of which workspace happens to be open) has no existing home. Candidate approaches, none clearly right yet:

1. **New table**, e.g. `user_settings` keyed by `user_id`, with its own PowerSync stream scoped to `auth.user_id()` instead of workspace membership, plus a client-side table/read-path outside the `blocks`/`Repo` abstraction. Matches the semantics but is the biggest lift and a new parallel storage substrate.
2. **A designated "home" workspace** whose blocks are special-cased to always sync regardless of the active workspace. Reuses the whole `Block`/`Repo`/typed-property stack (including `getPluginPrefsBlock`), but needs a rule for unavailability (offline before first sync, revoked membership) and a way to keep it from showing up as a normal graph in workspace-switcher UI.
3. **localStorage, best-effort** — what theme already does. Cheapest, but explicitly device-local, not synced — which undercuts the actual ask if "follow me everywhere" includes new devices.

## Migration question (open)

Whichever tier wins, users already have per-workspace values set today. Needs a precedence rule (global default with per-workspace override winning when present?) and a decision on what happens to values already stored per-workspace: backfill the global tier from somewhere, leave them all as silent overrides of a fresh global default, or require a one-time re-pick.

## Ask

This needs a design decision before implementation: (a) which specific settings/toggles move to a global tier (vim mode is the clear motivating case), and (b) where a global tier's storage lives, per the three options above (or another one). Opening as a design/architecture issue rather than a ready-to-build ticket.

title: Several fuzz suites claim Unicode coverage but generate ASCII only (fc.string() default)
description:
Found while fixing a false coverage claim in `packages/agent-cli/test/subtreeOutline.fuzz.test.ts` (PR #447, Codex review).

In the installed fast-check 4.9, **`fc.string()` defaults to `unit: 'grapheme-ascii'`** — printable ASCII only. Any suite whose docblock or test titles claim arbitrary/Unicode string coverage while calling unqualified `fc.string()` is asserting something it never exercises: no non-ASCII, no combining marks, no supplementary-plane or formatting characters. That's the failure mode this whole review round kept surfacing — a test that reads as thorough and isn't.

Fixed in `subtreeOutline.fuzz.test.ts` by setting `unit: 'binary'` explicitly. A repo-wide grep turned up the following, reported but deliberately NOT fixed in that PR (out of its scope):

- **`src/data/test/workspaceAccess.fuzz.test.ts`** — real match: an explicit "arbitrary unicode" claim over unqualified `fc.string()`. Highest-value one to fix.
- **`src/data/api/codecs.fuzz.test.ts`** — softer: "any string" test titles over the ASCII default. Codec round-trips are exactly where non-ASCII, surrogate pairs, and normalization edges matter, so this is probably worth widening on the merits, not just for accuracy of the claim.
- `src/sync/crypto/test/cryptoCodecs.fuzz.test.ts`, `aead.fuzz.test.ts` — non-issues; they correctly combine ASCII and binary units.
- `src/paste/test/splitMerge.fuzz.test.ts` — a comment states a wrong premise about the default, but the generation is harmless. Doc-only fix.

For each: either widen the unit to match the claim, or narrow the claim to match the generator. Widening is usually right for parsers/codecs/serializers; narrowing is fine where ASCII genuinely is the domain. Worth a quick check of whether widening surfaces real failures — if it does, those are findings, not reasons to keep the narrower generator.

title: Flaky: HotkeyReconciler real-timer hold test times out under full-suite load
description:
`src/shortcuts/test/HotkeyReconciler.test.tsx`'s real-timer hold test intermittently fails with a 5000 ms vitest timeout during full-suite runs (`pnpm run check`), and passes cleanly standalone (63/63).

Observed independently in two separate work streams during the PR #447–#454 batch, on branches that touch nothing in the hold path — so it's load/timing dependent, not caused by either change.

The test exercises the `phase: 'hold'` / `holdMs` mechanism with REAL timers, so under CPU contention from a parallel full-suite run the elapsed wall-clock can exceed the 5 s test timeout without anything being wrong with the code under test. That's the hypothesis, not a confirmed diagnosis — worth someone checking whether the hold assertion can be driven with fake timers (as the sequence-timeout differential in `sequenceMatcher.fuzz.test.ts` does) or polled on the outcome rather than racing a fixed budget.

Related but distinct: #455 (definitionSeeds deferred-pass test, different mechanism, same "only fails under full-suite load" shape). If someone picks these up together, the common theme is tests whose success depends on wall-clock progress inside a contended run.

title: Flaky: definitionSeeds deferred-pass test fails under full-suite load ("parent block does not exist")
description:
`src/data/definitionSeeds.test.ts` → "scheduled seed materialization (Repo wiring, §4.3) > materializes the active workspace registry seeds through the deferred pass" failed in CI on PR #448 ([job](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/actions/runs/30475446660/job/90655889561)), on a branch that touches only `src/services/uploadTransactionsWithFallback.fuzz.test.ts` — nothing in the seed path.

Isolated runs pass consistently (4/4 locally on that branch), so this is load/timing dependent, not a code defect on the PR.

Repeated stderr during the failure:
```
[seedMaterialization] workspace ws-seeds property seeds failed (will retry next open/seed change):
  parent block <uuid> does not exist
```

**Hypothesis, not established:** the deferred seed pass can run before the parent block its seeds attach to is committed/visible, and under full-suite CPU contention the "retry next open/seed change" fallback doesn't land inside the test's wait window. If that ordering is genuinely possible rather than a test-harness artifact, the same race exists in production — seeds would silently not materialize until the next workspace open or seed change. That fallback may well be the intended design, in which case only the test's wait needs to be made outcome-polled rather than timing-dependent. Someone who knows the deferred-pass contract should decide which it is before this is written off.

Worth checking together with the other intermittent seen in this file during the same batch of work (a network-dependent `ENOTFOUND proj.supabase.co` in a full-suite run) — a test in this file reaching for a real host is its own problem.

Reproduce by running the full suite under load (`pnpm run check`) rather than the file alone.

title: Restoring a daily note / journal / kernel page silently drops user-added extra aliases
description:
Surfaced while auditing PR #451 (issue #378). **Pre-existing on master — not introduced by that PR**, which is why it's filed separately rather than folded in.

The restore branches in `getOrCreateJournalBlock` / `getOrCreateDailyNote` (src/plugins/daily-notes/dailyNotes.ts) and `getOrCreateKernelPage` (src/data/kernelPage.ts) re-claim the domain's canonical alias set with an unconditional whole-list write:

```ts
await tx.restore(id, {content: JOURNAL_ALIAS})
await tx.setProperty(id, aliasesProp, JOURNAL_ALIASES)   // replaces the WHOLE list
```

`setProperty` on `aliasesProp` replaces the list rather than merging, so any alias the user added themselves — e.g. aliasing the 2026-06-11 daily note as "Standup notes" — is dropped when that page is restored. Repro: add a custom alias to a daily note → delete the page → navigate back to that date (which restores the tombstone) → the custom alias is gone, and any `[[Standup notes]]` wikilinks that resolved through it lose their binding.

Scope: only the RESTORE path. Live pages return early (`if (existing && !existing.deleted) return`) and keep their extra aliases; a fresh page has none to lose.

PR #451 does not change this end state — it strips the tombstone's alias bag before restoring so a stale claim can't abort the tx, but the canonical-set write on the next line was already clobbering extras. Fixing this means making the domain write a merge (canonical set ∪ existing user aliases) rather than a replace, which needs a decision about what "canonical" means when a user has deliberately removed one of the domain's own aliases — hence a separate issue rather than a drive-by change.

Related: the "squatter holds the block's CANONICAL alias" case that #378 / PR #451 explicitly leave as a domain decision, and the `needsRepair` unconditional-write path noted in that PR.

title: Duplicate-block payload selection in searchBlocksAcrossSources is order-dependent (3+ sources, missing timestamps)
description:
Found by the `searchBlocksAcrossSources` model-differential fuzz suite (PR #449, issue #432); the suite models the current behavior faithfully and documents it rather than pinning an intent the code doesn't implement.

`freshestCandidatePayload` (src/utils/linkTargetAutocomplete.ts) is a **pairwise** comparator applied as a running fold across all candidates sharing a block id:

```ts
if (typeof aTime === 'number' && typeof bTime === 'number' && aTime !== bTime) return aTime > bTime ? a : b
return a.score >= b.score ? a : b
```

Mixing a timestamp comparison with a score fallback makes it non-associative, so with 3+ candidates for one block id the surviving **payload** depends on source registration order. Hand-verified counterexample (same block id from three sources):

- A: `userUpdatedAt=10`, score 5
- B: `userUpdatedAt=20`, score 0
- C: `userUpdatedAt=undefined`, score 3

Fold in order A,B,C → `f(A,B)=B` (fresher), then `f(B,C)=C` (0 >= 3 false) → **C wins**.
Fold in order A,C,B → `f(A,C)=A` (5 >= 3), then `f(A,B)=B` (fresher) → **B wins**.

Same candidate set, different surviving payload. Note the final **score** is unaffected (it's a separate max) and which blocks appear / their ranking is unaffected — this is purely which copy of the block's payload is displayed.

Impact is narrow but it contradicts the function's own stated purpose ("newest `userUpdatedAt` wins ... so a stale index copy can't shadow live data just because it scored higher"): in the A,B,C order the no-timestamp candidate C shadows B, which has the newest timestamp in the set.

Suggested fix (design call, hence not done in the test PR): replace the fold with a total order — among candidates with a numeric `userUpdatedAt`, take the max timestamp; only if NO candidate has one, fall back to max score. That is associative and order-independent, and matches the documented intent. Whoever takes this should also decide what a candidate with no timestamp should mean when another candidate has one (currently: it can win on score).

When fixed, tighten the fuzz suite in `src/utils/test/linkTargetAutocomplete.fuzz.test.ts` — its model currently reproduces the running fold, and should become an order-independence assertion instead.

title: strength-tracker: in-progress workout doesn't pick up another device's set edits
description:
Raised by the Codex review on #438 ([thread](https://github.com/Stvad/knowledge-medium/pull/438#discussion_r3648251326)). Filed rather than fixed there, because the fix is a design change rather than a tweak.

## What happens

`TonightView` reseeds its draft only when the *identity* of the live workout changes — `liveIdentity` is block ids, deliberately. So if the same in-progress session is open on a second device and you tick a set or edit reps there, `liveWorkouts` changes but the identity string doesn't, and the already-open view keeps showing its own values. At Finish it writes its whole draft back, overwriting the other device's edits.

## Why it isn't a one-line fix

Including values in the reseed key would overlay remote values onto whatever you are typing right now — which is exactly what the ids-only key exists to prevent, and the primary use case is one-handed logging at 1am. Doing it properly means per-set dirty tracking: overlay a remote value only for sets this client hasn't touched since its last write, and leave locally-edited rows alone until they're flushed.

## Trigger for building it

Two devices logging the *same* session concurrently. Not observed yet — the realistic pattern is one device per session — so this is deferred rather than scheduled. If it does happen, the symptom is "a set I ticked on my phone came back unticked after finishing on the laptop".

## Sketch

- Track a per-set `dirty` flag set on local edit, cleared once `writeSet` resolves.
- On a live change, overlay values only into non-dirty sets (ids keep working as today).
- At Finish, write only dirty sets rather than the whole draft, so a clean row can't clobber a remote edit.

title: Document export/import round-trip drops all properties (importState replays only content/structure)
description:
### What

The `export_document` / `import_document` global actions (`src/shortcuts/defaultShortcuts.ts`) round-trip a document as JSON, but **properties do not survive the round-trip** — regardless of the properties-as-blocks flip.

`importState` (`src/utils/state.ts`) replays only `id` / `parentId` / `orderKey` / `content`:

```ts
const id = await tx.create({
  id: block.id, workspaceId,
  parentId: block.parentId ?? null,
  orderKey: block.orderKey,
  content: block.content,
})
```

and its input type `ParsedBlock` (`src/utils/markdownParser.ts`) has no `properties` field at all. So `properties` is silently dropped on import even though `export_document` serializes the full block rows.

### Why it's filed now (not fixed in PR #386)

Surfaced while wiring `export_document` to the visible outline in PR #386. It is **pre-existing and orthogonal** to properties-as-blocks — the loss happens under the cell model too. Noting it so it isn't mistaken for a props-as-blocks regression: exporting the visible outline (which #386 does) is correct precisely *because* the machinery representation is per-workspace derived state; the property *values* are lost by `importState` independently.

### Fix direction

Carry `properties` through `ParsedBlock` → `importState`'s `tx.create`. In a flipped workspace, `MATERIALIZE_PROPERTY_CHILDREN_PROCESSOR` would then rebuild the field/value children from the imported bag automatically (it watches `properties`), so no separate child-serialization is needed. Touches the live import path, so it wants an explicit decision before landing.

### Severity

P3: export/import is a manual power-user action, not a sync/backup path, and no data is *destroyed* (the source document is untouched) — the imported copy is just lossy.

title: V8 JSON.parse miscompile trips blockData round-trip fuzz (quarantined from deep tier)
description:
## Summary

`src/data/api/blockData.fuzz.test.ts`'s `blockToRowParams → parseBlockRow round-trips an arbitrary BlockData` property intermittently fails the nightly deep fuzz tier. Root cause is a **V8 `JSON.parse` engine miscompile**, not a product-code defect. Quarantined from the deep tier in PR #390 (pinned to a fixed-seed bounded sample); this issue tracks removing the quarantine once V8 is fixed.

## Why it's an engine bug, not a blockSchema defect

`blockToRowParams`/`parseBlockRow` are a pure `JSON.stringify` / `JSON.parse` round-trip — correct by construction. The observed failure: a `"` property key decodes to `\` (backslash). Evidence:

- The reported (shrunk) counterexample **passes on replay** — the property is non-deterministic w.r.t. hidden V8 state.
- Regenerating from the seed reproduces at exactly case 20420: `FUZZ_SEED=-915705129 FUZZ_RUNS=25000 yarn vitest run --testTimeout=600000 src/data/api/blockData.fuzz.test.ts -t "round-trips an arbitrary BlockData"`.
- Native, unpatched `JSON.parse` (`=== globalThis.JSON.parse`, `[native code]`). A standalone `node` parses the exact same string **correctly**; a same-shape hand-built string parses fine. Only this one ~486-char input, produced by `JSON.stringify` of a fast-check object, after the deep tier's heavy loop warms the engine, mis-parses.
- Reproduces in vitest and in standalone `node --jitless` (at case 20420); does **not** reproduce in standalone `node` (default JIT) or `--no-opt`.

## Status of upstream filing

No matching V8/Node issue found. Not yet filed upstream: I could not minimize it to a clean fast-check-free repro — hand-built strings with identical content don't trigger it, so it's tied to the specific internal string representation `JSON.stringify` emits plus process/JIT state. A fileable repro would need further reduction (or filed as-is with the fast-check script run under `--jitless`).

## Un-quarantine condition

Restore `fuzzParams(150)` on the property (drop `quarantinedFuzzParams`) once the upstream V8 fix ships in our pinned Node, and confirm the deep tier stays green with the reproducing seed.

See `docs/fuzzing.md` → "When the counterexample passes on replay".

title: Keybinding layers disagree about chord identity: dispatch-dead override spellings still strip live defaults
description:
Found by the PR #384 adversarial review (product-fix correctness lens), deliberately not fixed there (interface-adjacent).

**The gap.** tinykeys dispatch only understands `$mod` and literal `getModifierState` names (`Control`, `Meta`, `Alt`, `Shift`, case-sensitive) — spellings like `ctrl+x`, `cmd+k`, `option+a` never fire. But `canonicalizeChord` folds all of those, and `applyKeybindingOverrides` installs override keys RAW (rule-1 direct override) while using the canonical form for its collision-strip map. So the three layers disagree about what a chord *is*:

- **dispatch** (tinykeys, raw strings): `ctrl+x` is dead
- **strip map** (canonical): `ctrl+x` claims the `Control+x` bucket
- **conflicts UI** (canonical): same bucket

**Concrete failure.** Hand-authored override `ctrl+x` for action B → B's binding is dead at dispatch (pre-existing), but it also strips action A's live default `Control+x` → the chord now does nothing for anyone. Pre-#384 A still fired, so for this input class the (correct) canonical strip made things worse. The settings-UI capture path emits lowercase-but-tinykeys-valid spellings, so this bites hand-authored user prefs / plugin contributions, not captured ones.

**Suggested fix.** Canonicalize override `keys` once at ingestion — the canonical form (`$mod+…`, folded case after PR #384) is tinykeys-valid — so dispatch, strip, and conflict detection agree by construction, and a `ctrl+x` override actually fires. Touches what's stored/round-tripped for overrides, hence a deliberate decision rather than a drive-by: display currently shows the user's spelling.

Related: PR #384's canonicalizeChord case-fold (same review round) closed the `$mod+K`-vs-`$mod+k` slice of this.

title: Direct writes to `blocks` table don't trigger handle invalidation (stale in-memory cache)
description:
## Summary

Direct writes to the local `blocks` table (outside `repo.tx` and outside the sync ingress) do **not** trigger query-handle invalidation. Nothing watches `blocks`. The in-memory loader-handle cache (and any UI subscribed to it) goes stale until an unrelated overlapping invalidation fires or the client reloads.

## How invalidation actually works today

There are exactly two paths that produce a `ChangeNotification` → `handleStore.invalidate(...)`:

1. **Local writes** — synchronous, no observation involved. `repo.tx` records a per-id snapshots map during its primitives and, post-commit, calls `handleStore.invalidate(snapshotsToChangeNotification(snapshots, rules))` directly (`src/data/repo.ts:1164`).
2. **Sync writes** — PowerSync lands rows in `blocks_synced`; `AFTER INSERT/DELETE` triggers enqueue `(seq, id, op)` into `blocks_synced_changes`; the sync observer subscribes via `db.onChange({ tables: ['blocks_synced_changes'] })` (`src/data/internals/syncObserver/observer.ts:270`), drains the queue, materializes into `blocks`, and calls the **same** `snapshotsToChangeNotification` + `handleStore.invalidate(...)` (`src/data/internals/syncObserver/invalidate.ts:59`).

The only `onChange` subscription in the data layer is on `blocks_synced_changes`. There is **no** watcher, queue, or invalidation trigger on `blocks` itself.

This is deliberate — `src/data/internals/handleStore.ts:1026`:

> Note: `tables` is intentionally NOT auto-emitted. The `kind:'table'` dep mechanism is still wired through `handleStore.invalidate(...)`, but no production query depends on it — auto-emitting `['blocks']` on every commit walked the channel for nothing.

So the effective invalidation contract is: **a write is observed iff it goes through `repo.tx` or arrives via the `blocks_synced` sync ingress.** A raw `UPDATE blocks …` outside those paths fires no handle invalidation.

## Scope / nuance

- **SQL-side derived state stays consistent.** There *are* `AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` triggers on `blocks`, but they maintain derived tables (`row_events`, `block_aliases`, `block_types`, `blocks_fts`, `uploads`) — not handle invalidation (`src/data/internals/clientSchema.ts:419`–`925`). So a direct write keeps aliases / type index / FTS correct; only the **in-memory handle cache** goes stale. This is a stale-view bug, not data corruption.
- **Likely a regression introduced by e2ee Layout B (needs confirmation).** In a vanilla PowerSync setup the app reads from the PowerSync-managed table and `onChange`/`watch` (SQLite update-hook backed) fires for *any* write to it, including out-of-band SQL. Layout B split the read table (`blocks`, plaintext) from the sync table (`blocks_synced`, ciphertext), moving the watch to the sync ingress and re-plumbing local-write invalidation onto the explicit `repo.tx` call. The property "any write to the read table is observed" was dropped as a side effect. (The current gap is code-verified; the "this worked pre-Layout-B" comparison is inferred from PowerSync's default reactive model, not from reading the Layout-A code — should be confirmed.)

## Blast radius

Small in normal operation: all app code writes via `repo.tx`, and remote changes flow through `blocks_synced`. The only writers that hit the gap are **out-of-band raw SQL**: the agent bridge `sql execute`, `__omniliner.repo.db.execute`, manual debugging. Those can self-recover today by calling `handleStore.invalidate({ tables: ['blocks'] })` or reloading (the bridge has a `reload` verb).

## Options to consider

- **Do nothing / document the contract** — codify "writes must go through `repo.tx` or the sync ingress" as the invalidation contract; treat raw `blocks` writes as unsupported.
- **Symmetric trigger+queue on `blocks`** — add a `blocks_changes` trigger + a second `onChange` so local writes flow through the same queue as sync writes. Downsides: loses the synchronous, before+after-snapshot precision of the current `repo.tx` fast path (queue carries only id+op, throttled), so it would be a *fallback* for out-of-band writes rather than the primary path.
- **Make the agent bridge's mutating verbs self-invalidate** — have `sql execute` / `eval` emit a coarse `handleStore.invalidate({ tables: ['blocks'] })` (or reload) after a raw write, closing the most realistic real-world gap without touching the hot path.

## TODO

- [ ] Confirm whether pre-Layout-B (Layout A) actually observed direct `blocks` writes (verify the regression claim against the old code).
- [ ] Decide between documenting the contract vs. closing the gap (and at which layer).

title: Empty-plaintext envelope boundary (blank block content) is untested
description:
**Severity:** Low · **Area:** sync/crypto (envelope) · **Status:** confirmed (missing test) · **Audit:** `docs/correctness-audit-2026-06-18.md` (B5)

## Summary
The empty-plaintext envelope boundary (a blank block's `content`) seals to exactly the 28-byte floor (`NONCE_BYTES + GCM_TAG_BYTES`). The decode floor is `< 28` so it passes today, but nothing tests it — a future off-by-one (`<= 28`) would quarantine every empty block on download.

## Where
- `src/sync/crypto/envelope.ts` (`decodeEnvelope` length floor)
- `src/sync/crypto/aead.test.ts`, `envelope.test.ts` (never seal `''`)

## Proposed fix
Add a `seal('') → open === ''` round-trip test and a `decodeEnvelope` truncation test over `[0..28)` bytes to pin the floor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Test: empty-string content column round-trips (`open(seal('')) === ''`).
- [ ] Test: truncated envelopes below the floor are rejected.
- [ ] `yarn run check` green.

title: Workspace-key paste with internal whitespace/newline throws instead of being cleaned
description:
**Severity:** Low · **Area:** sync/crypto (workspace-key paste UX) · **Status:** confirmed · **Audit:** `docs/correctness-audit-2026-06-18.md` (B4)

## Summary
A workspace-key paste containing internal whitespace/newline (line-wrapped paste, printed-on-paper backup) throws `base32: invalid input` — only the outer string is trimmed. A valid backup looks corrupt. No data loss, but a recovery-UX failure for the exact "legible on paper / retyped" case the format is meant to support.

## Where
- `src/sync/crypto/base32.ts:17-23`
- `src/sync/keys/workspaceKey.ts:35` (only outer `trim()`)

## Proposed fix
Strip all internal whitespace from the WK string before base32-decode (in `parseWorkspaceKey`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Test: a WK with internal spaces/newlines parses to the same key as the unwrapped form.
- [ ] `yarn run check` green.

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): low-priority perf misc (logging, copy N+1, bootstrap writes)
description:
Lowest-priority unverified candidates from the 2026-06 audit.

1. **`serializeSelectedBlocks` issues one subtree SQL query per selected block (N+1) and can duplicate overlapping subtrees** — `src/utils/copy.ts:63` — multi-block Cmd+C runs N independent `subtree().load()` calls and emits overlapping descendant rows twice. Dedup by hierarchy (`validateSelectionHierarchy`) then fetch in one query.
2. **Independent get-or-create bootstrap page writes run strictly sequentially** — `src/bootstrap/workspaceBootstrap.ts:154-167` — Properties/Types/Recents pages have no mutual dependency yet are awaited serially on the TTI path; `Promise.all` them. Caveat: `repo.tx` serializes on the single wa-sqlite write lock, so the clear win is the warm path (overlapping 3 read round-trips) + collapsing stacked await latency. (Companion to the cold-start DDL round-trip issue.)
3. **`console.debug` string-building in the per-chunk upload path** — `src/services/powersync.ts:347` (also `:313`, `:326`) — argument expressions evaluated regardless of whether debug logging is surfaced; per-chunk (not per-row) so bounded. Gate behind a dev flag. Lowest priority.

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): bundle/build payload - minify, lazy-load tutorial extensions
description:
Unverified build/bundle candidates from the 2026-06 audit. (The two biggest individually-tracked bundle wins — `@babel/standalone` and the `lodash` barrel — have their own issues.)

1. **Unbundled, unminified build ships ~11.7 MB raw JS across 1,152 preloaded files with a 117 KB index.html** — `vite.config.ts:148` — `preserveModules:true` (load-bearing for extension `@/` imports) + `minify:false` (an independent choice) + `sourcemap:true`; the 117 KB HTML parses before boot and unminified JS is several-fold larger to transfer/parse. **Highest-leverage item in this group:** flipping `minify:false` (terser preserves export names, so module URLs/named exports are unaffected) is the cheap safe win; optionally bundle+minify the vendor subtree extensions never import by path. Confidence medium on the vendor-bundling half.
2. **Tutorial-only example-extension source strings (~15.5 KB) eagerly bundled into the startup chunk** — `src/extensions/exampleExtensions.ts:1` — pulled in via a static import in `defaultShortcuts.ts:35` (core startup) + `tutorial/outline.ts:19`; used only by the tutorial / a rarely-invoked action. Lazy-load with `await import('@/extensions/exampleExtensions.js')` inside the handler.

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): bulk sync/reprojection - window large passes & id loads
description:
Unverified candidates from the 2026-06 audit — two bulk passes hold large in-memory sets / unbounded txs instead of windowing like the download observer (`DEFAULT_DRAIN_CHUNK=1000`).

1. **`materializeWorkspace` loads every workspace id into one array before windowing** — `src/data/internals/syncObserver/observer.ts:227` — `SELECT id FROM blocks_synced WHERE workspace_id=?` with no LIMIT, held as one array (320k strings for a large workspace) for the whole windowed drain, partially defeating the "keep memory flat" intent. Page with a keyset cursor. Runs only on unlock/reconcile/recovery — rare.
2. **Whole-workspace ref reprojection runs in one unbounded `repo.tx`** — `src/data/repo.ts:1488` — `reprojectRefTypedProperties` funnels all matched rows through a single tx (builds the entire snapshots map in memory, holds the writer for the whole pass, emits one giant ps_crud tx), unlike the download observer which windows at 1000. Marker-gated/idle-deferred/add-only, so only bites the first cold start after a new ref-typed schema over a large graph. Window into chunks.

## Related
#91 (parallel reads for cold-start contention).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, bulk-ops group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): references/backlinks post-commit processing - batch lookups, avoid redundant second writes
description:
Unverified candidates from the 2026-06 audit in the references/backlinks post-commit processors.

1. **`parseReferences` resolves alias targets one-at-a-time with serial awaited DB lookups per content edit** — `src/plugins/references/referencesProcessor.ts:139` — N distinct wikilinks → N sequential awaited `aliasLookup` round-trips (plus a seat-probe on miss, `:152`) post-commit. Off the typing path and handle-cached, so bulk-paste of many distinct new wikilinks is the trigger. Batch with `WHERE alias IN (...)` or `Promise.all`.
2. **`normalizeReferences` same-tx processor issues a second full-row UPDATE (and second row_events row) when references are not canonical** — `src/data/internals/normalizeReferencesProcessor.ts:48` — short-circuited by `referencesEqual` when already canonical; compounds with the `tx.update` wide-SET issue and `row_events` (#132). Fix the wide-SET issue first (narrow SET) so this second write only touches `references_json`.
3. **Reference-changing edits trigger a second full commit-pipeline pass** — `src/plugins/references/referencesProcessor.ts:266` — a ref-set-changing edit opens its own `repo.tx` writing `{references}`, re-running the whole pipeline (a second `handleStore.invalidate` walk, a second `command_events` row, an extra ps_crud entry). Largely inherent to the deliberate post-commit-separate-tx design; the realistic mitigation is the inverted index (#80) + alias-batching, not removing the second tx. Recorded as structural cost, not a bug.

## Related
- The `tx.update` wide-SET issue (item 2 compounds with it).
- #80 (HandleStore inverted index — reduces item 3's cost).
- #132 (row_events write size).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, references group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): getEffectiveActions recomputed in hot dispatch/render paths
description:
Unverified candidates from the 2026-06 audit — the effective-action list (a nested action×transform loop + a fresh ~100-element array) is rebuilt in several hot paths instead of being read from a memoized source.

1. **Pointer/imperative dispatch re-runs the full transform+override pipeline (and re-allocates the list) on every click** — `src/shortcuts/HotkeyReconciler.tsx:242` — `dispatchPointerAction` / gesture dispatchers / `runActionById` (`runAction.ts:46`) each call `getEffectiveActions(runtime)` fresh, though `HotkeyReconciler` already holds the identical list memoized (`:158`). Read a memoized list via a ref, or memoize `getEffectiveActions` at module level keyed on facet identities.
2. **`MobileBottomNav` rebuilds the effective-action list + a Map on every render, and re-renders on every block focus change** — `src/plugins/mobile-bottom-nav/MobileBottomNav.tsx:50` — `getEffectiveActions` + `new Map(...)` in the render body; subscribes to `useActiveContextsState()` which changes on every focus/edit transition. `useMemo` keyed on `[runtime]`.
3. **`useRegisteredAction` runs the full effective-action pipeline in render with no memoization** — `src/plugins/left-sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:57` — `getEffectiveActions(runtime).find(...)` in render per `SidebarAction`; the sidebar renders only a handful and is a toggle surface, so impact is small. `useMemo` on `[runtime, actionId]` or rely on a module-level cache.

The clean fix for all three is one shared memoized `getEffectiveActions` keyed on facet identities (the reconciler already proves the memo key works).
