title: Perf audit 2026-06 (grab-bag): React render-path memoization & viewport-mount cleanups
description:
Lower-ranked render-path candidates from the 2026-06 audit, **not individually adversarially verified**. Grouped; each is independently actionable.

1. **No `React.memo` anywhere on the block render path** — `src/components/BlockComponent.tsx:16` — a structural edit invalidates the parent's `childIds` handle → `BlockChildren` re-renders → recreates every `<LazyBlockComponent>` → every mounted sibling re-renders down to a full markdown reparse. Confidence medium on the exact re-render trigger set; `React.memo(BlockComponent)` is safe and strictly beneficial. (This is the page-wide fan-out the markdown-reparse issue's medium-downgrade is conditional on.)
2. **Markdown render config reallocated with fresh identities every render** — `src/components/renderer/MarkdownContentRenderer.tsx:35` — fresh `remarkPlugins[]`/`components{}` + an O(references) wikilink Map rebuild per render; the structural blocker that keeps the markdown-reparse memo from being effective. `useMemo` keyed on `[resolveMarkdownConfig, block, blockContext, references]`. (Prerequisite for the markdown-reparse issue.)
3. **Wikilink display decorator runs unmemoized for every wikilink every render** — `src/plugins/references/markdown/wikilinks/Wikilink.tsx:28` — `resolveWikilinkDisplay` loops all decorators per wikilink per render; the daily-date decorator calls `parseLiteralDailyPageTitle` + `pickBlockDateAdapter` (each `canHandle` reads `block.peek()`). Memoize per `(alias, blockId)`.
4. **`useRenderer` runs an unmemoized registry filter+sort (incl. ReactPlayer URL regex) per block per content edit** — `src/hooks/useRendererRegistry.tsx:14-42` — explicit `'use no memo'`; `Object.values(registry).filter(canRender).sort(priority)` per render. Bounded by registry size (~13), constant-factor. Cache the choice keyed by `(rendererKey, types, context flags)`.
5. **`LazyViewportMount` keeps a live `ResizeObserver` per mounted block for its whole lifetime** — `src/components/util/LazyViewportMount.tsx:60-71` — a mounted block never reverts to a placeholder, so continuous observation (a forced `offsetHeight` read on every reflow) is wasted after the first measurement. Measure once or `disconnect()` after first non-zero measurement.
6. **`LazyViewportMount` module-level caches grow unbounded and force eager remount** — `src/components/util/LazyViewportMount.tsx:7-8,38,43` — `mountedCacheKeys`/`measuredHeights` are never pruned (leak) and always-eager-on-revisit (`:38`) re-incurs the O(N) initial-mount cost the lazy wrapper exists to avoid. Bound the caches; still gate mount on the IntersectionObserver.
7. **Per-block window resize/orientationchange listener even when no gesture recognizer applies** — `src/extensions/continuousGestures.ts:680` — `useSyncExternalStore(subscribeViewport, ...)` adds 2 window listeners per mounted block even when `recognizers.length===0` (desktop default), unlike the shared-listener pattern in `keyboardViewport.ts`. Gate on `recognizers.length>0` with a stable module-level no-op subscribe.

## Related
- The markdown-reparse issue (items 1–2 are its prerequisites).
- #74 (per-block flicker on lazy hierarchical loads — useTransition).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (unverified candidates, render-path group)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06: BlockCache snapshots - unbounded growth + redundant per-write JSON.stringify fingerprinting
description:
Two related issues in `src/data/blockCache.ts`.

## 1. Unbounded snapshot map (verified, low)
`src/data/blockCache.ts:95` — the per-id `snapshots` Map only removes entries on hard-delete (`deleteSnapshot`, `:186`) or `markMissing` (`:240`); every block loaded via query hydrate or `repo.load` stays as a deep-frozen full `BlockData` forever. Hydration paths (`repo.ts:440-453, 519, 888, 896`) add on every paged document, so a long-lived session accumulates without bound. `docs/perf-baseline.md:390-395` estimates ~3 KB/block (~150 MB at 50k blocks), **but** the memory bench came back GC-noisy and the doc flags it needs a steadier harness — magnitude unverified, and 50k distinct blocks in one uninterrupted session is the upper tail.

**Fix:** bounded LRU keyed on entries with no active `BlockCache.subscribe` listeners (`trackedIds()` at `:211` already exposes the seam, zero current callers). Eviction is lossless — the snapshot is written **after** the SQLite commit (`commitPipeline.ts` STEP 6), so the next read re-hydrates the identical value via `applyIfNewer`.

**One edge:** synchronous `block.data`/`peek()` readers (`hooks/block.ts:83-99`) holding a `Block` without subscribing would throw `BlockNotLoadedError` if their snapshot is evicted mid-use — "evict unsubscribed only" mitigates but doesn't fully eliminate this. Effort: medium.

## 2. Double full JSON.stringify per write (unverified candidate, low)
`src/data/blockCache.ts:14-15,128-143` (also `:132`) — `setSnapshot` does two full `JSON.stringify` of the whole block per cache write for dedup, including re-fingerprinting the *existing* snapshot though it can't have changed. `applyIfNewer` already gates on `updatedAt <=` before delegating, so only the local commit path genuinely needs the dedup.

**Fix:** store the fingerprint alongside the snapshot; skip it where the snapshots map already proves the row changed.

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (BlockCache eviction, verified; + fingerprint candidate, unverified)._

title: Perf audit 2026-06: block markdown re-parsed per render - confirm React Compiler doesn't already memoize before fixing
description:
## Location
`src/components/renderer/MarkdownContentRenderer.tsx:35` / `:39`

## ⚠️ Verify-first (cross-area disagreement)
The `react-rendering` audit area **retracted** this finding after running `babel-plugin-react-compiler` (enabled at `vite.config.ts:45`) on the compiled output and concluding the compiler auto-memoizes the `<Markdown>` element and `markdownConfig`. Two other areas verified the mechanism at source level but did **not** reconcile against the compiled artifact. **Before any manual fix, confirm against compiled output whether the React Compiler already memoizes this.** If it does, this is a no-op. If it doesn't (e.g. because the freshly-allocated config identity defeats the compiler's dependency tracking), the fix below applies.

## Problem
`MarkdownContentRenderer` calls `runtime.read(markdownExtensionsFacet)` then `resolveMarkdownConfig({block, blockContext})` on every render with no memoization (`:35-36`), then passes the result into react-markdown's synchronous `<Markdown>`. `resolveMarkdownRenderConfig` (`src/markdown/extensions.ts:29-53`) allocates a fresh `remarkPlugins` array + `components` object and invokes every extension factory each call (wikilink rebuilds a fresh `refMap` per call, `wikilinks/index.tsx:29`). react-markdown's `Markdown` export rebuilds the unified pipeline, re-lexes/parses, runs all remark transformers, and rebuilds the React tree on every call with zero cross-render memoization.

## Why it matters
Runs for any visible block whose parent panel/shell re-renders for an unrelated reason; amplified by breadcrumb/backlink panels that render a full `BlockComponent` per segment (`BreadcrumbList.tsx:86`). There is no `React.memo` in the `BlockComponent → DefaultBlockRenderer → ContentSlot → MarkdownContentRenderer` chain.

Severity: verified at source level, adjusted high → **medium**. The "full re-parse per keystroke" claim is **wrong** — the editing dispatcher (`plain-outliner/interactions.tsx:26-29`) swaps to the CodeMirror renderer while `inEditMode`, so `MarkdownContentRenderer` is not mounted for the block being actively edited; the re-parse happens once on edit-mode exit/commit, not per character. The remaining real cost is per-block re-parse on **parent-triggered** re-renders.

## Fix (if not compiler-handled; medium)
`useMemo` the `markdownConfig` keyed on the resolver identity (the facet `read` is cached per facet id, `facet.ts:188-189`) plus the reactive fields the extensions read — **content + references + workspaceId** (wikilink reads `data.workspaceId`; the original `[content, references, markdownConfig]` key is incomplete). Then wrap the `<Markdown>` subtree in a memo. The config-identity stabilization (tracked in the React render-path grab-bag) is a hard prerequisite — a memo keyed on the freshly-allocated `remarkPlugins`/`components` would never hit.

## Effort
Medium (gated on the verify-first step).

---
_From the 2026-06 performance audit (finding 8, verified at source level; see the cross-area note)._

title: Audit 2026-06: smaller verified observations (backlog)
description:

title: Audit A1 (rescoped): row_events is deliberate history — optimize storage / retention without losing reconstructability
description:
## Status (rescoped 2026-06-12)

Owner correction to the original audit finding: `row_events` is the **deliberate client-side history** — it stays, for all workspaces. The audit facts stand (zero runtime readers since `rowEventsTail.ts` was deleted in 588937cd; full before+after row JSON per write; the measured 262 MB / 304k-row growth case), but the conclusion changes: this is a storage-optimization-and-retention issue, not a remove-dead-machinery issue. Eventual work, not urgent.

## Optimization candidates — all must preserve full reconstructability

1. **Stop storing `before_json` where it's derivable.** The triggers see every write, so an event's `before_json` equals the previous event's `after_json` for the same row. Storing only `after_json` roughly halves the table while losing zero history. Caveats: each chain needs a base (rows whose first event predates trigger installation keep `before_json` on that first event, or get a one-time snapshot event), and any retention trim must keep a base snapshot per surviving chain.
2. **Stop re-embedding unchanged large columns** — `properties_json`/`references_json` are copied in full into both sides even when the write touched neither.
3. **Retention/compaction** — tracked in #75; high-watermark startup-DELETE sketch in `docs/row-events-retention.md`. Compact, never silently drop — history preservation is paramount.

## Trigger

Pick up when DB-size alerts from the health monitoring fire, or before targeting storage-constrained devices. The 262 MB case is the existing evidence of the growth rate.

Related: #75 (retention), #76 (local-only ps_crud).

---
*Source: audit finding A1 (`docs/architecture-audit-2026-06.md`), rescoped per owner correction 2026-06-12.*

title: Test-suite quality: remove source-literal tautologies & brittle over-mocking (audit follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to the test-suite audit. #107 already deleted many pure contribution-list / shortcut-string-restatement tests. The items below are the **tautologies and brittle mocks that survived** that pass — tests that restate a source literal (so they can never catch a real regression) or couple to an implementation detail (so they fail for the wrong reason).

> Per AGENTS.md: "don't add tests that just re-state the code." This is the inverse-direction cleanup.

### Source-literal restatements
- [ ] **`src/data/api/changeScope.test.ts:13`** — `Object.keys(CHANGE_SCOPE_POLICIES)).toEqual(Object.values(ChangeScope))`; the `satisfies Record<ChangeScope, …>` annotation already enforces this at compile time.
- [ ] **`src/data/blockSchema.test.ts:43`** — exact column-name-list `toEqual`. Keep only the `not.toContain` migration guards (~L58–60).
- [ ] **`src/data/internals/clientSchema.test.ts:~216`** — trigger-*name* inventory restatement. (#107 added trigger-*behavior* tests to this file but left the name list.)
- [ ] **`src/extensions/test/config.test.ts`**, **`src/plugins/geo/blockTypes.test.ts`**, **agent-cli `packageManifest.test.ts`**, and the **srs-rescheduling SM-2.5 parameter-list** assertion — same restate-the-constant pattern.

### Over-mocking / brittle coupling
- [ ] **`src/data/internals/kernelMutators.test.ts:296`** — `vi.spyOn(TxImpl.prototype, 'childrenOf')` then asserts not-called; passes silently if the method is renamed or inlined.
- [ ] **`src/extensions/test/discoverToggleTree.test.ts:125`** — `toEqual(['system:dup', 'system:dup'])` *codifies* accidental non-dedup; a future real dedup fix would fail this for the wrong reason.
- [ ] **`src/components/BlockProperties.component.test.tsx`** — asserts a raw `'fixed'` CSS class string (couples the test to styling).

🤖 Tracked from the test-suite audit · https://claude.ai/code/session_01Qb9hPUtry6z6YrC4hf9EyB

title: Consider DB/query revisioning if dirty-load handle semantics become hard to reason about
description:
## Problem

`LoaderHandle` treats in-flight loads that observe a matching invalidation as **dirty** for subscriber publication: the dirty result may still satisfy the original `load()` promise and update the internal cache, but subscribers rebuild only from the clean follow-up reload. This is intentionally conservative and cheap.

## Current state (verified)

The dirty-load model is in place and unchanged in `src/data/internals/handleStore.ts` (mid-load invalidations set `pendingReinvalidate` and schedule a post-settle reload). There is **no** monotonic DB/query revision/version counter.

## Longer-term shape (only if this area keeps producing edge cases)

Add a monotonic DB/query revision model. Every local commit and row-events-tail apply advances a revision; query loads carry the revision they read; handles publish only results whose read revision is at least the latest matching invalidation revision. That makes freshness explicit and could avoid redundant dirty reloads when a load is provably already fresh.

Costs: thread revision accounting through repo txs, sync-applied invalidations, query loaders, and tests; dynamic deps still need the existing "changes during load" queue unless queries can declare every relevant dep before SQL.

**Trigger:** do this only if the dirty-load generation model becomes ambiguous in practice.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3 — deferred until trigger)._

title: Investigate referencesProcessor.test.ts schema-swap flake
description:
## Problem

`src/plugins/references/test/referencesProcessor.test.ts > parseReferences — schema-swap reprojection > removes stale field refs when a property stops being ref-typed` fails intermittently in the full suite but passes in isolation (`yarn test --run src/plugins/references/test/referencesProcessor.test.ts` is green). Observed once during the navigation refactor on master @ `cf397f0`. The failing assertion checks `references_json` for a stale `target-a` ref that should have been removed when the `reviewer` property was retyped away from `block-ref`.

## Current state (verified)

The test still exists (no `.skip` / `.only`), asserting via the existing `vi.waitFor(...)` quiescence pattern on `references_json`. No new retry / timeout / quiescence logic has been added — the flake is not yet patched.

## Direction

The shape suggests an ordering race: alongside the rest of the suite, the property-type cleanup fires before/after the assertion's `vi.waitFor` window in a way the in-isolation run doesn't trigger. Likely candidates: a shared trigger-flush queue across tests in the same vitest worker, or a `repo.tx` racing the schema-swap delete.

Worth instrumenting next time it fails: dump `references_json` history for `src` plus the `row_events` trail across the swap window. If the pattern matches `cycle-detection-test-flake.md`, the fix may be the same shape (await processor quiescence before asserting).

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3)._

title: Block-id keying for properties_json + kernel-schemas-as-blocks
description:
## Problem

Companion to the schema-rename follow-up (#72). The longer-term direction is to key `properties_json` by the schema block's **id** rather than its name. That removes rename fragility everywhere properties are stored or referenced, and lines up with the user-defined-types "type id = block id" decision.

## Current state (verified)

- `properties_json` keys are property **names** (`src/data/block.ts` reads `data.properties[schema.name]`).
- `getSchemaForBlockId` exists (`src/data/userSchemasService.ts`) but resolves **user-defined** schemas only (blocks of type `property-schema`). Kernel/plugin schemas (`defineProperty` in code) have no backing block and no synthetic ids.

## Open sub-questions before committing

- **Kernel/plugin schemas without backing blocks** need either: **synthetic deterministic ids** (`uuid-v5(kernel:status)`, resolved via a registry, source-of-truth stays in code — lowest cost) or **full materialization** (a property-schema block per kernel schema per workspace — composes with all block machinery but moves source-of-truth to data + raises plugin-unload lifecycle questions). Middle path: ship synthetic ids now; the same id space can back materialized blocks later.
- **Migration cost.** Every existing `properties_json` blob needs rekeying — one-shot pass at workspace open; version the workspace so old clients don't write back name keys.
- **DB readability.** Raw `properties_json` becomes opaque (`{"a3f9-…": "open"}`); mitigate with a tooling pretty-printer that resolves ids via the schemas table.
- **Properties-as-blocks (Tana-style) is a different question** — that means each VALUE is a block (real per-read indirection). Block-id keying just renames JSON keys; reads stay 1× Map.get.

## Acceptance

1. Kernel/plugin schemas resolve through the same `getSchemaForBlockId` path as user schemas (synthetic or materialized — pick one).
2. `block-type:properties` refs work uniformly across all schema kinds, replacing the Phase-1 "hide kernel schemas in the picker" workaround.
3. `properties_json` migration runs once at workspace open; idempotent.
4. The schema-rename follow-up (#72) is satisfied as a side effect (renames touch labels, never keys).

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3)._

title: Tighten render-surface model — replace open flag bag with a renderSurface enum
description:
## Problem

The render-surface model on `BlockContextType` (`src/types.ts:79`) is an open flag bag: `isNestedSurface` (umbrella) + specific descriptors `isEmbedded` / `isBacklink` / `isBreadcrumb`, set by each non-document mount and consulted via `useIsFocalRender(block)` / `isFocalRender(ctx)`. This was the smaller initial fix for the embed-of-focal-block bug — it composes in nested cases and adding a surface only means setting the umbrella.

## Current state (verified)

`BlockContextType` still carries `isNestedSurface?` + `isEmbedded?` / `isBacklink?` / `isBreadcrumb?` (plus a `[key: string]: unknown` catch-all). `useIsFocalRender` checks `!isNestedSurface`. No `renderSurface` enum.

## Tighter shape (when triggered)

Replace umbrella+descriptor flags with a single `renderSurface: 'document' | 'embed' | 'backlink' | 'breadcrumb'` enum (Option B in `docs/render-surface-vs-flags.html`). Pros: real type-system enforcement, mutually-exclusive states modeled as such, surfaces discoverable from a union. Cons: closed set needs amending when a surface lands; nested cases collapse to innermost-wins rather than composing (theoretical today — none of the five focal-affordance sites discriminates outer surface).

Adjacent ideas worth pulling from `docs/renderer-resolution.md` if revisited: pass `renderSurface` (or a frame slot) as an explicit `BlockComponent` prop ("the mount site already knows"); separate dispatch metadata from React component identity (static `canRender`/`priority`); explainability/reason chains.

**Trigger to revisit:** a fourth render surface (preview pane, sidebar peek), OR the flag bag's open-set ergonomics produce a real bug (someone forgets to set `isNestedSurface` on a new mount).

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3 — deferred until trigger)._

title: rendererProp silently no-ops on a misspelled / unregistered renderer id
description:
## Problem

`useRenderer` reads `rendererProp` and only honors it via `if (rendererKey && registry[rendererKey])` (`src/hooks/useRendererRegistry.tsx:26`). When the prop names a renderer id that isn't registered (typo, plugin not loaded, renderer renamed), the lookup silently fails and resolution falls through to the `canRender` predicate sort. The user's explicit override is lost with no signal.

## Current state (verified)

`src/hooks/useRendererRegistry.tsx:26-28` — `if (rendererKey && registry[rendererKey]) { return registry[rendererKey] }` then proceeds to alternatives with no `console.warn` and no placeholder.

## Fix shape

When `rendererKey` is set but absent from the registry, `console.warn` with the offending id + the available ids, and either (a) render a "renderer not found" placeholder so the lost override is visible, or (b) fall through with the warning. Pick **(b)** for now — less disruptive — but at least surface it. Independent of any larger renderer-resolution redesign; cheap fix.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3). Good first issue — small, self-contained._

title: Id-only collection handles for subtree / ancestors / backlinks
description:
## Problem

`repo.childIds(id)` was added alongside `repo.children(id)` to give callers that only need the structural list a handle whose only dep is `parent-edge` — child property updates don't invalidate it, and the loader is a lighter `SELECT id` query (`core.childIds`, `declareRowDeps: false`). `useChildIds` / `useHasChildren` were rewritten on top of it.

The same id-only shape would work for the other three list-handle factories (`subtree`, `ancestors`, `backlinks`) since their React consumers all use `Block` facades for per-row reactivity, making the per-id `row` deps redundant. But the leverage drops sharply:

- `subtreeIds` — same shape of win in principle, but **no current hot consumer**. Wait for an actual callsite.
- `ancestorIds` — Breadcrumbs is the only consumer; chains are O(depth) shallow and need block content anyway.
- `backlinkIds` — Backlinks UI renders each backlink's content; row deps bounded by list size. (Note: `backlinksForBlockQuery` already returns `string[]`, but that's a plugin-level choice, not a derived variant.)

## Current state (verified)

- `childIdsQuery` exists; `subtreeQuery` / `ancestorsQuery` / `manyAncestorsQuery` still return full `BlockData[]`. No id-only variants.

## Direction

Add when a measured hot path appears, not preemptively. Phase 4's `queriesFacet` (`tasks/data-layer-redesign.md` §13.4) is the canonical home — `repo.childIds` migrates alongside `repo.children` to `repo.query.childIds` with no downstream callsite changes.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3 — deferred until a measured hot path appears)._

title: Inverted dep-index in HandleStore.invalidate
description:
## Problem

`HandleStore.invalidate` walks **every registered handle** linearly on each invalidate, then walks **every dep** of each candidate inside `matches()`. This is perf-baseline's #1 open recommendation.

Why it may be worth doing sooner than the headline numbers suggest: many minor UI interactions are DB writes — selection changes, expand/collapse, property-panel toggle, focus moves. Sub-ms per walk × ~100 writes/sec during scroll/drag is real; the 10–20 ms band of savings is meaningful at that frequency.

## Current state (verified)

- `src/data/internals/handleStore.ts`: `invalidate()` iterates a snapshot of all handles, calling `h.matches(change)` → `matchesAgainst(this.deps, change)` (per-dep walk). No inverted `Map<bucketKey, Set<Handle>>` index.
- Softeners already landed: per-handle dedup at `ctx.depend` (commit `62e913cf`) and `repo.metrics().handleStoreInventory` (commit `1b4e8937`, exposing `handleCount`, `totalDeps`, `maxDeps`, `p50/p95Deps`, `topHeavy[]`).

## Index shape (when it's time)

`Map<bucketKey, Set<RegisteredHandle>>` keyed per dep kind: `row:<id>`, `pe:<parentId>`, `ws:<workspaceId>`, `tbl:<table>`, and `p:<channel>\x00<key>` for plugin deps (today's hottest family). Maintained inline in `onDep` (add) and `dispose` (remove). **Bucket-membership-is-sufficient**: at invalidate, union the touched buckets and invalidate every handle in the union — no `matches()` confirmation pass needed. That's the real win (skips the per-dep walk that dominates for fat handles).

Triggers to re-check (now measurable in `repo.metrics()`):
- `handlesWalked / invalidations` ratio > ~200 in real sessions
- `handleStoreInventory.handleCount` materially above ~500 during normal use
- `maxDeps` over ~1000, or `p95Deps` growing toward max
- `mutate.setContent` p95 / per-tx-flush time degrading
- a scroll/drag/multi-select flame graph shows `invalidate()`/`matches()` on the critical path

Correctness surface: `runLoader` dep-replacement on settle must diff old vs new and patch buckets atomically; mid-load live-publish must update buckets in the same step as `deps.push`; `dispose` must remove from every bucket; add an `inflightHandles` Set so `observeDuringLoad` becomes `O(inflight)` not `O(N)`. Acceptance: drive `scripts/bench/bench-handles.ts` `(N=…, 1 match)` and `setContent with M bystanders` rows to constant time.

_Triaged from `docs/follow-ups.md` (P3 — deferred until a measured trigger fires)._

title: searchSourcesFacet: cross-source score is uncalibrated — reconsider it as the payload tie-break
description:
Deferred design call surfaced while fixing the duplicate-payload merge (GH #450 / PR #449). Unreachable today: core.content is the only registered source.

facets.ts asks each source to map its confidence onto core's rough 0-300 text-relevance scale, with NO per-source normalization at the merge point. Core's own scale is exact=300 / prefix=200 / substring=100-index, plus a recency boost up to +80.

That is tolerable for RANKING (an already-shipped decision). It is shakier as the payload TIE-BREAK, where 'higher score wins' can mean 'we displayed a stale copy because an uncalibrated number from a different scale came out larger'. A vector source's cosine 0.82 mapped to 246 is not commensurable with core's weak-substring 96.

If we do not trust cross-source scores for this, registration order (core first) is a more honest tie-break: equally deterministic, and explainable to a plugin author.

Note this interacts with the authority-declaration issue — if payload authority becomes a source declaration, the score tie-break mostly stops mattering.
